# #0009 — A3: Jolt harness + substitution
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [S1] [S4] [A3] [21] [44]   opened: A3   closed-by: 5605e65 (A3 engineering complete; A3.6 signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07)
deps: blocks #0018

A3 deliverable (kickoff §2): Jolt pinned with `CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC=ON`;
`det_math` backing swaps libm → Jolt math (S1 FROZEN here); capsule mechs
articulated with Jolt constraints present the same `IBodyState`/actuation
interfaces the stub presented (S4 FROZEN here); A2's test suite re-runs on Jolt
bodies. Melee benchmark harness scaffold (21) stands up.

## Tests — A3 gate checklist (expanded on phase entry, 2026-07-24)

Decomposed into six sub-workorders (A3.1–A3.6). Each is delegated to one subagent
and top-level-reviewed before the next is released (same cadence as M2–M7). All
commits ref `#0009`. A sub-workorder that surfaces an ambiguity / bug / freeze gets
its OWN issue per the §5a taxonomy — this list does not create new milestone issues.

**A3.1 — Jolt toolchain (foundation)** ✅ commits 71f597c, a73d73e
- [x] Jolt pinned via CMake `FetchContent` to **v5.6.0** + commit hash,
      `CROSS_PLATFORM_DETERMINISTIC=ON`, SSE4.2-only ISA, single-threaded, under
      `-ffp-contract=off`. Pin recorded in `cmake/jolt.cmake`.
- [x] Jolt determinism smoke test: rigid pendulum, 300 ticks, world hash
      bit-identical two-runs AND gcc-vs-clang (`0x28c1abbd508e27fb`). Reproduced.

**A3.2 — `det_math` S1 swap** ✅ commit 718ba72 (S1 ready-to-freeze → #0025)
- [x] `det_math` backing swapped libm → own inline deterministic double
      sin/cos/exp/log + `sqrtsd` intrinsic; NO libm in simcore, enforced by
      `tools/lint_determinism.py` in CI. (Jolt trig is float-only/no-pow — #0024.)
- [x] `dm::pow` = `pow(E,·)` = `exp`; `exp` added to the seam; every `dm::` caller
      deterministically backed.
- [x] A2 suite green under the swap; gcc-regen == clang-regen == committed corpus,
      byte-identical (reproduced). SIM_VERSION_TAG → `a3-detmath-v1`.
- [x] S1 ready-to-freeze reported via freeze-request **#0025** (human-gated).

**A3.3 — Articulated capsule mech behind `IBodyState`** ✅ commits e17e6f8, f47bab6
- [x] `JoltMech` (trunk capsule + 2 feet + 2 ankle constraints, ~50 t/12 m) presents
      the frozen `IBodyState` + `CopCommand` exactly; STANDS under the real controller
      (torque-only, gcc==clang `0x97f71cff03e77400`, falsification: topples without
      control). S4 seam extracted to permanent Jolt-free `core/body_iface.h`.
- [x] Driven by the SAME L1/L0 (reads only `IBodyState`, actuates only `CopCommand`);
      no Jolt type in `loco/` (grep-enforced). CoP→actuation map documented in #0026.

**A3.4 — Substitution proof (the heart of A3)** ✅ commits 7591b8f, c5e15a8, 06321bb, 2302e8d
- [x] A2's behavioural suite re-runs on Jolt bodies: stand ✓, walk 50 m ✓, halt-as-plan
      ✓ [56], absorb mid-stride shove ≤L1 ✓ [57], large-shove escalation ✓ (exactly 1),
      hash-earns-its-keep ✓ (M6, [49]). Orderings hold; magnitudes retuned (sanctioned).
      Walk-law gained the angular-momentum channel (#0028=(B), rung 0 of #0029).
- [x] Per-test replay bit-identical gcc vs clang (all Jolt hashes match). NOTE: the
      Jolt **golden corpus** (regression files) is DEFERRED to Phase B per the #0028
      ruling — do not baseline goldens on a mech pending the articulated-legs decision.

**A3.5 — Melee benchmark scaffold (constraint 21)** ✅ commit bfad67e
- [x] `tools/bench_melee` stands up N `JoltMech`s (own PhysicsSystem each — the S4
      seam doesn't expose it; shared-system is the Phase-B melee benchmark) walking
      headless; wall-clock tick-time vs mech-count measured (observational only, sim
      stays deterministic — `det_hash` reproduced). **First Jolt baseline** (§5, not a
      target): clean-linear **~98–108 µs/mech/tick** through N=64, ~10× headroom vs the
      20-mech/33 ms target; the eventual limit is contact-pairs (Phase B), not N. GPU
      never used [44].

**A3.6 — Seam freezes + deferred-to-A3 decisions surfaced for sign-off**
- [x] **simcore ISA pinned** (SSE4.2, matching Jolt; the cross-machine-hardening note
      below) — commit follows; corpus byte-identical, gcc==clang unchanged (verified).
      *(The engineering item; the rest of A3.6 is human sign-off.)*
- [x] **S1 FROZEN** (#0025) and **S4 FROZEN** (#0018, complete surface incl.
      `IActuatedBody` + `support_half_width`) — signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07.
- [x] #0014 (double-vs-float): ratified — **double** in simcore, Jolt float at the
      phys boundary. Also ratified: #0024 det_math backing (B), #0026 CoP map (A).
- [x] #0019 (gravity source): ratified reading **(A)** — ω from the charter constant.
      Plus #0027 principled `feas_L1` (support_half_width) landed (5605e65) & closed.

## Notes
- Blocked until M0–M7 green. Jolt-in-UE tutorials pending upload gate Phase C, not this.
- **Jolt acquisition decision (2026-07-24):** CMake `FetchContent`, pinned to
  **v5.6.0**, commit `e77f175595e64cb44218cc9d9d56fc365ad0e36a`
  (`https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics`). Chosen over submodule/vendored for a
  recorded, reproducible pin with no submodule bookkeeping; the exact version+hash
  is what enters the replay file per constraint 3. Network reaches the repo from
  this environment (verified). Redirectable by the human before A3.1 lands.
- **Cross-machine gate — scope limit of A3-here:** the true Phase-A exit gate wants
  bit-identity *across two machines/compilers*; this environment is one machine, so
  A3 certifies the **gcc-vs-clang two-compiler proxy** + repeat-run identity. True
  multi-machine reproduction needs human-owned infra and is NOT claimed closed by
  A3's local green. Flagged, not silently narrowed.
- **det_math swap task (surfaced at M4):** `simcore/loco/stepper.cpp` uses
  `dm::pow(E, ωT)` for the LIPM `e^{ωT}` propagation (E = full-precision literal),
  and the seam declares `dm::pow`. When the S1 backing swaps libm→Jolt math, the
  Jolt-backed `det_math` MUST provide a deterministic `pow`/`exp` (Jolt's surface is
  primarily Sin/Cos/Sqrt) — either back it deterministically or refactor the loco
  propagation off `pow`. Verify no `dm::pow`/`dm::exp`/`dm::tan`/`dm::asin`/`dm::acos`
  caller is left without a deterministic Jolt backing before the cross-machine gate.
  **RESOLVED at A3.2** (commit 718ba72): `det_math` now backed by our own inline
  deterministic double sin/cos/exp/log (+ `sqrtsd` intrinsic, IEEE bit-ops); no
  libm anywhere in simcore, enforced by `tools/lint_determinism.py` in CI. `exp`
  added to the seam; all 13 `pow(E,·)` sites still call `pow` (reroute→exp deferred,
  logged in #0024). Ambiguity #0024 + S1 freeze-request #0025 opened, human-gated.
- **FOLLOW-UP surfaced in A3.2 review (simcore ISA not pinned):** the cross-compiler
  determinism of `det_math`/simcore relies on gcc and clang emitting the same FP
  instructions. They do **on this one machine** under baseline SSE2 + `-ffp-contract
  =off` (proven: gcc-regen == clang-regen == committed corpus, byte-identical). But
  only *Jolt's* targets are pinned to an explicit ISA (SSE4.2, in `cmake/jolt.cmake`);
  **simcore's own compile flags are not ISA-pinned**. For the true cross-*machine*
  gate, simcore must be pinned to one explicit ISA too, or a machine defaulting to
  different codegen (x87, auto-AVX/FMA) could diverge. Do this as part of A3.6 /
  the cross-machine hardening, before any real multi-machine claim.
gate:a3.title: A3: Jolt harness + substitution

# #0010 — A4: the server-authoritative control layer (Rev 2)
type: milestone        status: closed        closed-by: signed off by DayZee 2026-08-09 (Phase-A close batch)
refs: [S7] [A4] [9] [10] [11] [12] [44] [45]   opened: A4
deps: blocks #0011

REWRITTEN 2026-08-08 to Framework Revision 2 (#0032). The original A4 — "control tree +
stock firmware; fixed 300 ms / 9-tick delay pipeline; in-sim skill hooks; 50 m-walk-across-
two-machines exit test" — is SUPERSEDED. Git history holds the old version verbatim; this
file is what A4 actually is now. (We are not pretending the plan didn't change; we changed
it, on the record, via #0032.)

## What A4 delivers (Rev 2)
The **server-authoritative control layer** — the tooling that ALL command-and-control flows
through. Three parts:

- **THE BUS = permissioned channel pub/sub** (#0033): SENSOR / ACTUATOR / GOAL / CONTROL
  channels. Pilot intent is held **H** (config) ticks; **only ACTUATOR-channel writes are
  recorded/replicated**; sensors, goals, and conflicts are server-side owner-private. S7
  freezes here once the bus reflects #0033.
- **THE CONTROLMATRIX** (#0036) = the **root** command-and-control fabric: every script
  connects to the world through it (reads sensor channels, writes actuator channels); it does
  server-side per-channel conflict resolution; roles/permissions come from a SuperAdmin
  **metaTooling device**; conflicts go to a private conflict channel. Only the **resolved**
  actuator writes reach the recorded stream — a replica replays them and reproduces the
  physics without re-running any script (privacy + client==server fidelity).
- **SCRIPTS through a location-transparent contract** (`observation → actuator writes`,
  deadline-bound): imperative or neural, local or remote (cloud-GPU). The stock walker
  (`wbc`/`stepper`) is one imperative script; nets are the same shape.

**Canonical Rev-2 design set:** #0032 (what changed & why) · #0033 (the bus) · #0036 (the
ControlMatrix) · #0029 (movement-control architecture: floor / scripts / contractual handoff).

## Gate checklist (Rev 2)

**A4.1 — the bus as permissioned channels (S7 freezes here)**
- [x] command bus + **H-hold** delay + `SERVO_SETPOINT` vocabulary — commits 8258f8b, bf08740.
- [ ] the full **channel** model per #0033 (SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL as first-class
      channels; actuator-only recording). Then S7 ready-to-freeze under Rev 2 (#0030, human-gated).

**A4.2 — the ControlMatrix (#0036)**
- [x] **v1**: root fabric, server-side per-channel priority resolution, private conflict
      channel, and the privacy/replica proof (two writers contend; a replica reproduces the
      physics from the resolved writes ALONE) — commit 3b94858, gcc==clang, CI green.
- [ ] **v2**: **engagement-leases** (a role, when engaged, holds its channels and suppresses
      lower streams whether or not it writes, until disengaged — #0036 refinement) + the
      **SuperAdmin metaTooling device** (roles / permissions / delegation).

**A4.3 — scripts through the contract**
- [x] the stock **imperative** walker (`wbc`/`stepper`) runs as a script; its resolved writes
      are the recorded stream — replica-split experiment, commit 864fd33.
- [ ] a **neural / remote-shaped** script through the SAME contract — proves the location-
      transparent seam (the step toward cloud-GPU scripts).

**A4.4 — the exit test = 50 m walk, replica-faithful  (RULING: option iii — DayZee 2026-08-08)**
- [ ] The Jolt mech walks **50 m** under ControlMatrix control (walking script → resolved
      actuator writes → servo → physics), and a **replica reproduces the 50 m walk from the
      recorded actuator writes ALONE** — bit-identical (client==server), gcc==clang (the
      cross-machine proxy). No script re-run on the replica.
- [ ] The recorded actuator stream includes **foot placement as an actuator channel** (the
      replica-split experiment proved splines+feet reproduces bit-identically; #0033 allows
      actuator "device commands"). This makes the CURRENT (leg-less) mech's walk replica-
      faithful WITHOUT articulated legs. Phase B later replaces the teleport-style foot
      placement with real joint setpoints — the test's shape is unchanged, only what PRODUCES
      the foot-placement writes.
- **Ruling:** DayZee chose **(iii)** — keep the real 50 m walk as the A4 exit, made replica-
  faithful via the ControlMatrix + the fidelity requirement ("use it to make it work" — the
  fact that it works IS the proof the flexibility is there). NOT re-scoping to leg-less-only
  (i); NOT pulling articulated legs #0028 forward (ii).

## Notes
- `deps: blocks #0011` — Phase B begins when A4.4 passes CI.
- Delay is now **H+R config** (no fixed 9/3); **tick rate stays 30 Hz** (#0032 decision).
- Superseded design (git-only): the pre-Rev-2 A4.1–A4.4 (fixed pipeline, control-tree+firmware,
  in-sim skill hooks). The control tree (`control_tree.cpp`) is superseded-in-role by the
  ControlMatrix (#0036) but left in the tree.

---

## CLOSED by DayZee Christopher Reay, 2026-08-09 — the A4 exit gate is met.
The milestone closes on its EXIT GATE (A4.4), which passed at commit 0b6f36b: the Jolt
mech walks 50 m under ControlMatrix control and a replica reproduces all 820 ticks
bit-identically from the recorded actuator writes ALONE (server==replica
`0xbe392e4055107282`, gcc==clang). Both halves of A4.3 landed — the IMPERATIVE walker
(`wbc`/`stepper`) and the NEURAL script (`neural_script.h`, commit 1c51f95,
`NEURAL_SCRIPT_HASH=0x2ebaf9b4a5c1f6db` gcc==clang) — proving the `IScript` contract is
made-of-agnostic. ControlMatrix v1 (#0036, commit 3b94858) is the resolver. The
server-authoritative + deterministic-replica model (Rev 2) is proven end-to-end.

**Two gate-checklist items are DEFERRED to Phase B (#0011), their natural home** — both
are better motivated once there is real multi-script contention to arbitrate:
- **A4.1 full channel model** (SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL as first-class channels).
  S7 (#0030) freezes when this lands — so S7's freeze also moves to Phase B (NOT frozen
  at this close; the recorded surface is explicitly non-final per #0032/#0033).
- **A4.2 v2** (engagement-leases + the SuperAdmin metaTooling device).

Phase A is functionally and formally complete. `deps: blocks #0011` releases — Phase B opens.
gate:a4.title: A4: the server-authoritative control layer (Rev 2)

# #0004 — M3: L1 whole-body controller on degenerate plan
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [S4] [M3] [45] [49] [57]   opened: M3   closed-by: 97d7ef5

M3 deliverable (loco brief §6, §11): L1 balances on `Remain` (degenerate gait).
S4 (`IBodyState` + actuation channels) is ready-to-freeze at M3; FROZEN at A3.

## Tests
- [x] Stands 60 s on `Remain`.
- [x] Small impulse (Δv = 0.05 m/s) absorbed by ankle strategy alone — no escalation (L0-absorb) [57·L0].
- [x] `wbc_step` signature requires PreviewWindow; no overload without it [45].
- [x] All L1 state lives in `GaitFsm` → hashed [49].
- [x] `feas_L1()` analytic 1-step capturability predicate present.

## Notes
- `test_m3_balance` green (all 4 milestone executables pass; clean under
  `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -ffp-contract=off`). `ctest`: 4/4 pass.
- **Files**: `simcore/loco/wbc.{h,cpp}` (L1 whole-body controller + `feas_L1`),
  `simcore/loco/loco_world.h` (the reusable composed L1+L0 world, reused M4–M7),
  `simcore/tests/test_m3_balance.cpp`, `simcore/CMakeLists.txt` (+`loco/wbc.cpp`,
  +`test_m3_balance`). Extended `simcore/loco/loco_types.h` GaitFsm (see below).
  No change to `core/`, `stubphys/`, or `servo.{h,cpp}` (rate-crossing untouched).
- **Preview mandate [45]** enforced twice: the ONLY entry point is
  `Setpoints Wbc::wbc_step(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&, GaitFsm&) const`
  — `preview` is a required by-const-ref parameter with no default and no
  preview-omitting overload; and `PreviewWindow` cannot represent "no plan" (a
  `static_assert(!is_default_constructible)` in the test proves it).
- **All L1 state in GaitFsm [49]**: the WBC (`Wbc`) holds only hashed *config*
  (`WbcParams`); every cross-tick *state* item lives in `GaitFsm` — `phase`,
  `phase_t` (dwell clock, advanced each tick), plus the M3 additions `prev_xi`
  (capture-point warm start) and `step_retime` (the ±2-tick L1-retime field). All
  hashed; `GaitFsm` is registered (id 5) in `LocoWorld`.
- **Control law**: DCM/capture-point ankle law `p = x_ref + (1 + k_dcm/ω)(ξ − x_ref)`,
  `ω = √(g/h)`, `k_dcm = 2ω`, CoP clamped to the support segment; hip flywheel
  realizes any clamp residual as `τ = g·m·(p_unclamped − p_clamped)` (inert while
  ξ ∈ support). CoP reference from the preview = stance location for a Remain.
- **Absorbed impulse (b)**: Δv = 0.05 m/s along the support (Y) axis → ξ peak
  0.03566 m (theoretical Δv/ω = 0.03910 m) vs support half-width 0.600 m (5.9 %);
  hip torque stayed ≤ 8.2e-11 N·m (idle vs the 2e5 N·m authority) → **ankle alone**;
  `feas_L1` never failed → **no escalation**; CoM recovered to 1.3e-12 m of stance.
- **Step-timing mechanism [57·L1]**: the ±2-tick bound + `GaitFsm.step_retime`
  field exist but are INERT on a Remain terminal (no step to retime); the request
  source lands at M5. Not over-built.
- **feas_L1 source-agnostic [57a]**: `bool feas_L1(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&)`
  — no parameter through which a disturbance cause could arrive; verifiable by
  signature alone.
- **ω reconstruction**: `IBodyState` exposes `com_height()` (h) but not gravity;
  ω = √(g/h) reconstructs g from the charter constant (`WbcParams.gravity`;
  `feas_L1` file constant). Logged as ambiguity #0019 (conservative reading).
- S4 (`IBodyState` + actuation channels) ready-to-freeze reported via #0018
  (scheduled freeze event is A3, not M3, per the seam table).

- Halt: closed-form fixed-step deceleration, ξ error → 0 over exactly k steps

# #0006 — M5: recovery ladder rungs L0–L1
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M5] [57]   opened: M5   closed-by: aca6203

M5 deliverable (loco brief §9, §11): the bottom two rungs of the recovery ladder.
A mech absorbs a mid-stride shove without escalating past L1; a large shove
escalates exactly once.

## Tests
- [x] Mid-stride impulse Δv = 0.15 m/s → absorbed via step-timing adjustment, plan intact, no escalation past L1 [57·L1].
- [x] Large impulse (tuned Δv = 10.0 m/s) → `feas_L2` fails → exactly one `EscalationReason{layer=2}` recorded.
- [x] Ladder predicate signatures take (IBodyState, PreviewWindow) only — source-agnostic by signature [57a].
- [x] Ordering invariant holds: absorb < in-stride < escalate.

## Notes

### What was built (bottom two rungs + escalation RECORDING, not consumption)
- `simcore/loco/ladder.{h,cpp}`: `ladder_eval(IBodyState, PreviewWindow) -> LadderResult`,
  the per-tick BOTTOM-UP evaluation run AFTER L1. feas_L1 → feas_L2, stop at first
  failure. Semantics: feas_L1 holds ⇒ L0/L1 absorb (no escalation); feas_L1 fails but
  feas_L2 holds ⇒ L1 in-stride catches it in-plan (no escalation); feas_L2 fails ⇒
  RECORD `EscalationReason{layer=2}` (L2 plan repair is NOT built — that is M6).
- `feas_L2` redefined stance-anchored: ξ is 2-step reachable iff within N·foot_reach
  (= 2·3.0 = 6.0 m) of the CURRENT stance. Anchoring to the body (not to the already-
  deadbeat-replanned preview footholds) is what makes an un-catchable shove DETECTABLE
  — the planner chases ξ with placement but not beyond kinematic reach.
- `simcore/loco/wbc.cpp`: the L1 in-stride step-timing law made ACTIVE. Closed form,
  no tolerance loop, no current-tick input (signature-clean). resid = (ξ − ξ_prop)·d̂,
  ξ_prop = p + (ξ_prev − p)·e^{ω·DT} (exact single-support LIPM flow); on the periodic
  orbit resid ≈ 0 (inside a deadband ⇒ retime 0 ⇒ steady walk untouched), a shove spikes
  it. Quantized through a deadband and CLAMPED to ±2 ticks; a forward shove ⇒ touch down
  earlier (advance, −retime). Gated off on the touchdown-tick stance switch. GaitFsm gains
  `prev_stance` + `warm` (hashed).
- `simcore/loco/stepper.cpp`: footholds CLAMPED to `foot_reach` of the foot they step
  from (`clamp_to_reach`). Feet cannot teleport — inactive on the steady gait (stride
  0.9 m << reach 3.0 m; M4 unchanged) and active only when a disturbance throws the
  deadbeat target beyond reach. This makes feas_L2 meaningful (placement cannot chase a
  ξ that escaped the reachable set) and makes a large-shove escape SUSTAINED (one onset,
  not a fail/recover/fail oscillation).
- `simcore/loco/loco_world.h` (WalkWorld): the escalation stream — a hashable
  `std::vector<EscalationReason>` registered at id 12 (with its edge-trigger state); the
  ±2-tick retime applied to `frame_.next_touchdown` once per step (id 11 gains the latch).
  Escalations recorded on the RISING EDGE of infeasibility (one structured reason per
  onset). No handler above L2 exists — recorded, not consumed [S8 PROVISIONAL].

### Source-agnostic signatures (verbatim, no cause parameter)
    bool         feas_L1(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
    bool         feas_L2(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
    LadderResult ladder_eval(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
Asserted at compile time in test_m5 via exact function-pointer types.

### Tuned magnitudes + capturability numbers (ω = √(9.81/6.0) = 1.2782)
Stub landmarks: ankle half-width 0.6 m (L0); 2-step reachable radius N·foot_reach =
2·3.0 = 6.0 m (feas_L2).
- absorb   Δv = 0.05 (M3): ξ excursion 0.05/ω = 0.039 m  < 0.6  → L0 ankle absorbs.
- in-stride Δv = 0.15     : ξ excursion 0.117 m; feas_L1 marginal (fails 141× post-shove),
                            feas_L2 holds; step-timing engaged (retime −2 at the shove
                            tick); 0 escalations; mech walked on to x = 17.5 m. (brief
                            value, KEPT.)
- escalate  Δv = 10.0     : ξ excursion 7.82 m > 6.0 m — escapes the 2-step reach. Exactly
                            ONE layer-2 escalation, verified robust across shove ticks
                            30–44 and windows 200/400/900. TUNED UP from the brief's 0.6
                            (excursion 0.47 m — trivially in-stride for this 50-ton, 6 m,
                            3 m-reach stub) per brief §11 ("tune to the stub's actual
                            capturability numbers; preserve the ordering"). Ordering in
                            ξ-excursion: 0.039 < 0.117 < 7.82; against landmarks 0.039 <
                            0.6 and 7.82 > 6.0.

### Escalation counts asserted
- test (a) in-stride: 0 escalations (layer ≥ 2 count = 0).
- test (b) escalate : exactly 1, {layer=2, predicate_id=feas_L2, budget=6.0, margin<0}.

### Determinism
Escalation buffer + edge state + retime latch all hash_into (registered ids 11/12); the
large-shove scenario replays bit-identically (test b-det). No `float`, transcendentals via
det_math (dm::pow(E,·)), all timing integer-tick, fixed-iteration. M0–M4 unchanged.

# #0007 — M6: hash-earns-its-keep (firmware state is load-bearing)
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M6] [3] [49]   opened: M6   closed-by: 8a22146

M6 deliverable (loco brief §11): prove `[49]` is load-bearing — that controller
state inside the hash catches divergence a physics-only hash would miss.

## Tests
- [x] Construct two runs whose physics states coincide at tick T but whose `GaitFsm` differs → assert tick hashes differ at T.
- [x] If the test cannot be constructed, document why in the test file. (N/A — the dynamic construction WAS achievable; see Notes.)

## Notes (M6 delivered — `simcore/tests/test_m6_hash.cpp`)

**Construction (dynamic, bit-reproducible).** Two identical `LocoWorld` stands on a
`Remain` terminal (the M3 stand: feet on ±Y, CoM offset 0.05 m). Run B's controller
is perturbed mid-stand via the new `LocoWorld::fsm_mut()` test hook.

**Perturbed field: `GaitFsm::phase_t`** (the gait dwell clock), `+= 0.5 s` injected
just before tick 50; observed at **T = 120**.

**Why physics stays bit-identical (⇒ physics-only hash matches).** The emitted
`CopCommand`/`SplineSet` is a pure function of (body state, preview, `WbcParams`).
In `Wbc::wbc_step`, `phase_t` is ONLY WRITTEN — the single line
`fsm.phase_t = fsm.phase_t + DT` — and is NEVER READ to compute the CoP, the hip
torque, or the ±2-tick step-timing (that block is gated `!preview.is_terminal()` and
reads `prev_xi/prev_stance/warm`, never `phase_t`). So the offset never enters the
setpoints ⇒ both bodies integrate identical commands each substep ⇒ physics is
bit-for-bit identical. Because `phase_t` merely accumulates (+DT/tick), the injected
offset PERSISTS unchanged to T (chosen over `step_retime`, which is inert on a Remain
terminal but is recomputed to 0 each tick, so it would not survive to a later T). This
is exactly the [49] case: a diverged controller state that HAS NOT YET acted on the body.

**Result (registry ids: id 2 = body dyn state = PHYSICS; id 5 = `GaitFsm` = CONTROLLER).**
- FULL tick hash at T=120 — **DIFFER**: A=`0x39bdd4ae0962c275`, B=`0x3deb41c3e57ba881`.
- PHYSICS-ONLY hash at T=120 — **MATCH**: A=B=`0x760125dc0e6e4ea2`
  (`LocoWorld::physics_only_hash()` folds body config id 1 + body state id 2, excluding
  the `GaitFsm`). This proves that WITHOUT folding the `GaitFsm` the divergence would
  pass silently — i.e. [49] is load-bearing.
- The property is asserted at every tick from injection to T, not only at T. A unit-level
  lemma over `HashRegistry` (identical body + differing `GaitFsm`) corroborates it.

**Test hooks added to `simcore/loco/loco_world.h`** (test-support, not a seam; hashed
state unaffected): `GaitFsm& fsm_mut()` (inject the controller-only divergence) and
`uint64_t physics_only_hash() const` (the physics-only contrast digest).
gate:m6.title: M6: hash-earns-its-keep (firmware state is load-bearing)

# #0008 — M7: replay corpus + CI regression
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M7] [3] [4]   opened: M7   closed-by: 4f452dc

M7 deliverable (loco brief §10, §11): the committed replay corpus and the CI
regression primitive (re-run corpus, diff hash logs). Closes the Phase A A2
stub-first locomotion slice (M0–M7).

## Tests
- [x] Replay corpus committed: stand / walk-halt / shove-absorb / shove-escalate.
- [x] CI job re-runs the corpus and fails on any hash-log mismatch.
- [x] Replay file format = {scenario id, seed, version tag, command stream}; per-tick hash log alongside.

## What landed
- `simcore/replay/replay.{h,cpp}` — the replay-file format + `serialize_replay`/
  `parse_replay` (deterministic, human-diffable, byte-stable round-trip: fixed
  field order, `%.17g` lossless floats), plus the pinned version tags.
- `simcore/replay/scenarios.{h,cpp}` — the INTERNAL scenario registry (not a
  seam; a small explicit 4-entry table per kickoff doctrine 2, NOT a generic
  engine) + `record`/`replay`.
- `simcore/tests/test_m7_corpus.cpp` — THE CI regression gate (runs under ctest
  → tools/ci.sh).
- `tools/record_corpus.cpp` — the REGEN path (executable target `record_corpus`).
- `corpus/` (repo root) — committed `<id>.replay` (inputs) + `<id>.hashlog`
  (golden per-tick hash log) for each of the 4 scenarios.

## Notes

### Replay file format (`ReplayFile`)
`{ uint32 format_version; string scenario_id; uint64 seed; string sim_version_tag;
vector<Command> commands }` where `Command = { uint64 tick; Kind{PLAN_INTENT,
SHOVE}; PlanIntent intent; Shove shove }`. `kReplayFormatVersion = 1`.
`SIM_VERSION_TAG = "s3-stub-v1"` — pinned in one header (`replay.h`); a deliberate
sim change that legitimately moves the goldens must bump it (the tag rides in
every replay file, so a stale corpus is self-identifying). `seed` is carried but
UNUSED: there is no RNG in S3 — it is pinned for format forward-compatibility
(constraint [3]), never a branch on sim logic. The S7 command-bus / 300 ms delay
pipeline is Phase A4 (brief §12): in S3 each command is applied UNDELAYED at its
stated tick.

On-disk layout (line-oriented, labelled tokens for diffability):
```
format_version 1
scenario_id walk-halt
seed 0
sim_version_tag s3-stub-v1
command_count 1
command 90 PLAN_INTENT kind HALT vel 0 0 0 halt 11.199999999999999 0 0 stance 0 by_tick 210
```

### The 4 scenarios (each lifts a known-good milestone setup; the initial stance
+ initial intent are baked into the builder keyed by scenario_id — the command
stream carries only the mid-run PlanIntent/Shove commands):
- `stand` (1800 ticks, M3 a): LocoWorld on a Remain plan, feet on the Y support
  axis (±0.6 m), 5 cm CoM offset. No commands. Behaviour: the offset is nulled
  (final |com_y| < 1e-3).
- `walk-halt` (400 ticks, M4): WalkWorld cruise 3 m/s on the periodic orbit; one
  command — PLAN_INTENT halt-at (x=11.2 by tick 210) at tick 90. Behaviour:
  decelerates to the Remain terminal, at rest (|vx| < 1e-2), no escalation.
- `shove-absorb` (300 ticks, M5 a): WalkWorld walk 1.8 m/s; one SHOVE Δv=0.15 m/s
  (7500 N·s +X) at tick 37. Behaviour: absorbed in-stride, ZERO layer-2
  escalations, keeps walking (final x > 10 m).
- `shove-escalate` (400 ticks, M5 b): WalkWorld walk 1.8 m/s; one SHOVE Δv=10 m/s
  (500000 N·s +X) at tick 37. Behaviour: ξ escapes the 2-step reach → feas_L2
  fails → EXACTLY ONE layer-2 escalation.

### Where the corpus lives
`corpus/` at the repo root (8 files: `<id>.replay` + `<id>.hashlog` ×4). The path
is compiled into the test and the regen tool via `MK_CORPUS_DIR`
(`${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/corpus`) so it resolves from any build dir (incl. a fresh
`rm -rf build`).

### Regen command (only on an INTENDED sim change; bump SIM_VERSION_TAG then)
```
cmake --build build --target record_corpus && ./build/simcore/record_corpus
```

### How the gate fails
`test_m7_corpus` parses each `.replay`, `replay()`s it, and `diff_logs` against
the golden `.hashlog`; a mismatch is a build break and prints the FIRST DIVERGING
TICK (the hash-diff bisector's atom). It also asserts the replay text round-trips
byte-exactly, the `sim_version_tag` matches, and each scenario's known behaviour
still holds (e.g. shove-escalate records exactly one layer-2 escalation) so the
corpus is meaningful, not merely self-consistent. This realises the A1/M0 "CI job
that replays the corpus" requirement now that there is real content.

### S3 slice status against constraint numbers (kickoff §5/§13 report)
The A2 stub-first locomotion slice (M0–M7) satisfies, at STUB fidelity:
- [1] fixed 30 Hz lockstep tick + [2] 120 Hz physics substeps — `core/tick.h`, held across every milestone.
- [3] state hash + versioned replay file — M0 hasher/registry; M7 full replay-file format + `SIM_VERSION_TAG`/`format_version`.
- [4] headless CI replay corpus hash-matches every commit — M7 `test_m7_corpus` under `tools/ci.sh`.
- [44] plan-driven control (WBC consumes a PreviewWindow) / [45] preview mandate — M3, type-enforced (no default-constructible PreviewWindow).
- [46] two-rate cascade, exactly one structure (SplineSet) crosses the boundary — M3/M4 worlds.
- [47] L0/L1/L2 layering — M2/M3/M4.
- [48] canonical ascending-id ordering — every world's HashRegistry; no container-iteration nondeterminism.
- [49] the tick hash covers controller state (GaitFsm), not just physics — M6 proves it is load-bearing; M7 hashes escalation stream + gait clock too.
- [56] preview never empty (illegal-empty unrepresentable) — M4 (b), type + runtime assert.
- [57] recovery ladder L0 absorb / L1 in-stride / L2 escalate, source-agnostic — M3/M5; the ordering absorb < in-stride < escalate is the invariant, reproduced by the corpus.
Seams frozen at stub fidelity: S1–S6, S8 (S8 provisional). DEFERRED to later
phases (NOT this slice): S7 command-bus/300 ms delay (A4), Jolt substitution
(A3, S4 real impl), terrain/Lua/UE (Phase B+). No RNG yet ([3] seed pinned/unused).

hold:consideration-replay-tiers-permissi.text:
# #0035 — Consideration (DEFERRED): replay tiers = permissioned data-exposure levels
type: ambiguity        status: open
refs: [44] [45] [S7]   opened: rev2-controlmatrix-design   closed-by: <design decision, when replays are built>
deps: informs #0032; informs #0033

Aside raised by DayZee during the ControlMatrix design (2026-08-08). NOT to be built now
— logged so it isn't lost.

A replay is just **recorded channel traffic**, so "who sees what in a replay" is the SAME
permissioned-channel model (#0033) applied to a recording. There is not one replay — there
are TIERS, each a default data-exposure policy, further gated by the viewer's relationship
to the mech (owner / opponent / spectator):
- **Fidelity replay** — resolved ACTUATOR writes + physics ONLY. Any viewer. Reproduces the
  motion (client==server gate), reveals no control internals. This is the minimal shipped stream.
- **Competition replay** — physics + an agreed-limited slice; opponents' control internals
  (scripts, sensors, conflicts, roles) stay PRIVATE, so a match can't be mined to reverse-
  engineer an opponent's controller.
- **Training replay** — the FULL data flow (sensors, conflicts, script I/O, roles) — owner only,
  for training/debugging their own scripts.

Ties directly to the Rev-2 privacy decision: what ships to other clients is only the resolved
actuator writes; the full internal data flow is server-side + owner-private. Replay tiers are
how much of that private flow a recording exposes, and to whom. Decide when replays/spectating/
competition are actually built (post-ControlMatrix). Doctrine: log it, don't build it.
hold:consideration-replay-tiers-permissi.title: Consideration (DEFERRED): replay tiers = permissioned data-exposure levels

hold:cop-to-jolt-actuation-mapping.text:
# #0026 — Ambiguity: CoP command -> Jolt articulated-body actuation mapping
type: ambiguity        status: closed
refs: [S4] [A3] [44]   opened: A3.3b   closed-by: signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07
deps: informs #0018

## Constraint / source conflict
The S4 seam (`core/body_iface.h`) hands the body a `CopCommand`:
```
struct CopCommand { Vec2 cop; Vec2 hip_torque; };
```
The throwaway `StubBody` realises this as an IDEALISED analytic model
(`stubphys/body.cpp::integrate`): a Linear Inverted Pendulum with a
finite-support centre-of-pressure plus a torque-limited hip flywheel, per
horizontal axis, decoupled:
```
c'' = w^2 (c - p) - tau/(m h)      p = CoP clamped to support,  w^2 = g/h
l'  = tau
```
There the CoP is a pure abstraction (a point the LIPM accelerates away from) and
the hip torque changes an abstract flywheel momentum with a direct CoM reaction
`-tau/(m h)` — nothing rotates, nothing contacts.

On the REAL articulated Jolt body (A3.3b: trunk capsule + two point feet joined by
ankle point constraints, dynamic under real gravity + real ground contacts) the
SAME `CopCommand` must become genuine actuation — ground-reaction / ankle / hip
torque on real bodies. The seam text itself flags this: *"Real Jolt bodies will
consume joint torques instead — same IBodyState read side."* But it does NOT pin
WHICH mapping. There are several faithful-looking choices, and they are not
equivalent on a real body:
- **CoP realisation.** (i) redistribute the vertical ground-reaction force across
  the two feet so the load-weighted CoP equals `cop`; (ii) an equivalent ANKLE
  TORQUE `tau_ankle = W*(cop - p_foot)` (the ZMP<->ankle-torque equivalence:
  shifting the CoP a distance d from the ankle is worth an ankle torque `W*d`);
  (iii) a horizontal shear force at the feet.
- **hip_torque mapping.** (a) a real torque on the trunk about the horizontal
  axes (the trunk physically leans — a true hip/ankle strategy); (b) an abstract
  reaction-only term that never rotates the trunk (literal stub emulation).
- **Reference frame.** the pendulum ankle/pivot reference for the CoP torque:
  the support-segment midpoint (ankle line) vs the live CoM vs the planned stance.

These readings differ physically. (ii)+(a) makes balance emerge from actuating the
real body against real gravity/contacts; a naive alternative — apply a horizontal
force at the CoM equal to `m·w^2·(c-p)` — would merely REPRODUCE the LIPM
acceleration analytically (a "cheat" that bypasses the real dynamics). The two are
indistinguishable in the stub but opposite in spirit on a real body.

## The readings
- **(A) Ankle+hip TORQUE on the trunk (implemented).** Map the command to a single
  torque applied to the trunk about the world horizontal axes:
  ```
  ankle_ref = support-segment midpoint (the ankle line, world x/y)
  tau_ankle = W * (cop - ankle_ref)          W = mass()*g   (ZMP<->ankle torque)
  ctrl      = tau_ankle + hip_torque         (per horizontal axis)
  T_worldY  = -ctrl.x   (sagittal / x-plane tip control)
  T_worldX  = +ctrl.y   (lateral  / y-plane tip control)
  AddTorque(trunk, {T_worldX, T_worldY, 0})
  ```
  Gravity and the ground contacts are REAL (Jolt integrates them); the injected
  torque is the ONLY actuation. Balance is a genuine inverted-pendulum problem —
  the falsification test (controller off => topples) proves it.
- **(B) Foot-force redistribution for the CoP** + trunk torque only for the hip.
  More literally "centre of pressure", but requires closed-loop control of the
  contact normal forces (which Jolt determines), i.e. an inner force-tracking loop
  — more machinery, same balance behaviour at this fidelity.
- **(C) Literal stub emulation:** an external horizontal CoM force reproducing
  `m·w^2·(c-p)` and a reaction `-tau/(m h)`. REJECTED — this is the analytic cheat
  the workorder forbids; it would make the "stand" prove nothing about the real
  body.

## Conservative reading taken (doctrine 6)
**(A) — ankle+hip torque on the trunk.** Rationale:
- **It is the faithful realisation of the stub's intent, not an emulation of its
  numbers.** The stub's CoP is "where the ground reaction acts"; the exact
  ZMP<->ankle-torque equivalence turns a CoP offset from the ankle into the ankle
  torque `W*(cop-ankle_ref)`. The hip flywheel term is the same *kind* of angular
  actuation as a real hip/ankle torque, so carrying `hip_torque` verbatim onto the
  trunk is the honest reading of "consume joint torques instead".
- **The linearised closed loop matches the model the controller assumes.** For an
  inverted pendulum of height ~h pivoting at the ankle, applying torque tau gives
  `x'' ~= (g/h)x - tau/(m h)` — exactly the stub's LIPM form (the destabilising
  `(g/h)x` here is REAL gravity, not injected). So `Wbc`'s DCM law + `Servo`'s PD
  drive it with the same sign/scale they used on the stub, UNCHANGED. Verified: it
  stands 10 s, CoM excursion ~1 cm, converging to the stance.
- **It is not a cheat.** No force reproduces the LIPM acceleration; the CoM only
  moves because the injected torque tips the real trunk about the real ankle
  constraints against real gravity. Disable the controller and the same mech
  topples (tick ~86 of 300) — the balance is demonstrably active.

## What was implemented (A3.3b, refs #0009)
- Topology: static ground; a dynamic vertical **trunk capsule** (46 t; charter §4
  capsule r=1, cyl=10 -> 12 m; CoM at z=6, mass-weighted CoM ~5.53 m); two dynamic
  **box feet** (2 t each) resting on the plane at (0, +/-0.6, 0.15); two **ankle
  point constraints** pinning trunk<->foot at each foot centre. Trunk + 2 feet =
  50 t (== `BodyParams.mass`). The two ankles lie on the Y support line, so the
  trunk's only free rotational DOF is a **sagittal (X-plane) tip** — a genuine
  inverted pendulum that topples unactuated. The lateral (Y) axis is base-supported
  by the segment (as a real biped's lateral stance is), so the lateral CoP/hip
  authority is near-inert at the stand equilibrium.
- Actuation: reading (A) above, per substep, then a fixed-dt single-threaded
  `PhysicsSystem::Update` (DT_SUB, 4 collision steps).
- Reference frame: `ankle_ref` = support-segment midpoint. Sagittal control comes
  through `hip_torque.x` (the CoP.x term is ~0 because the ankle line has no
  x-extent — the CoP cannot help sagittal tip, so the HIP must, exactly as in the
  stub's standing branch); lateral control is `W*(cop.y-ankle_ref.y)+hip_torque.y`,
  near-zero at equilibrium.

## Blast radius / awkwardness (signal for A3.4)
- **CoP has no sagittal authority** on this topology (feet aligned in x), so the
  whole sagittal balance rests on the HIP torque channel, which `Servo` clamps to
  `torque_law` budget (k*volume = 8e4 N·m by default) — a tighter authority than
  the stub's `tau_max=2e5`. Small perturbations are held; a large sagittal shove
  will saturate the hip sooner than the stub's abstract flywheel would. A3.4's
  shove/ladder tunings may shift (sanctioned by kickoff §2); orderings must not.
- **Lateral axis is base-supported, not a free LIPM.** The stub is a free LIPM in
  BOTH axes; the real segment support makes the lateral CoM nearly rigidly held, so
  the lateral CoP channel does little observable work at a stand. Faithful to a real
  biped, but a divergence from the stub model to keep in mind for walk (A3.4), where
  lateral CoP/foot-placement does real work.
- **hip torque physically leans the trunk** (real rotation) rather than spinning an
  abstract massless flywheel with a pure CoM reaction. Same stabilising effect at
  small angles; the trunk's real orientation now carries state the stub never had.

## Why this is logged, not silently resolved
The mapping from an idealised LIPM CoP+flywheel command to real articulated-body
actuation is a genuine modelling fork with a persistent consequence (it fixes how
EVERY real-body scenario in A3.4 actuates, and which balance authority each channel
carries). Choosing (A) over (B)/(C) is defensible and demonstrated, but it is a
decision a human should ratify. It **informs #0018** (the S4 freeze): the seam's
READ surface is unchanged and honoured by a second implementation, but the
actuation SEMANTICS of `CopCommand` on a real body are now concrete and should be
on the record before S4 freezes. This issue does not resolve #0018 and does not
change the seam shape. **Human-gated closure:** confirm reading (A) (ankle+hip
torque, ZMP<->ankle-torque equivalence, support-midpoint reference), or direct (B)
(explicit foot-force CoP), and rule on whether the sagittal/lateral authority
asymmetry above needs a topology change (e.g. a foot offset in x) before A3.4.

---

# #0024 — Ambiguity: det_math backing — "only Jolt math" vs Jolt float-only/no-pow vs the double mandate
type: ambiguity        status: closed
refs: [S1] [A3] [2]   opened: A3.2   closed-by: signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07
deps: informs #0014

## Constraint / source conflict
- The A3 plan text (loco brief §1 rule 2; kickoff §2 seam table) says the S1
  `det_math` swap moves the backing to **"only Jolt math (Sin, Cos)"** — i.e. the
  intent was that Jolt's deterministic math is what backs the seam after A3.
- But the concrete Jolt surface (verified against v5.6.0, the pinned commit):
  - `JPH::Sin/Cos/Tan/ASin/ACos/ATan/ATan2` are **FLOAT-only**
    (`Jolt/Math/Trigonometry.h`);
  - the only double routine is `JPH::Sqrt(double)` (`Jolt/Math/Math.h`);
  - **Jolt has no `Pow` and no double `Sin`/`Cos`.**
- Our seam is mandated **double** (#0014 conservative reading B: double throughout
  the sim), and the seam has 13 `dm::pow` call sites — every one is `pow(E, x)`,
  i.e. `e^x` for the LIPM `e^{ωT}` capture-point propagation. Jolt provides neither
  a double transcendental nor any `pow`.

So "back the double seam with Jolt math" is not literally satisfiable: routing
double→Jolt-float would (a) collapse the mandated double fidelity to float, and
(b) still leave `pow`/`exp` unprovided.

## The two readings
- **(A) Collapse to Jolt-float.** Take "only Jolt math" literally: call
  `JPH::Sin/Cos(float)` for trig and improvise `pow` (e.g. `exp` via `expf`/a float
  poly). Honours the plan's *words* but **breaks the double fidelity contract**
  (#0014-B) and still has no native `pow`.
- **(B) Own inline deterministic double implementations.** Back the
  transcendentals with our own scalar-double routines — the *same technique class*
  as Jolt's `Vec4::SinCos` (range reduction + minimax/Taylor polynomial), widened
  to double — compiled under the repo's `-ffp-contract=off` / no-fast-math on the
  pinned ISA. Honours "only Jolt math" in **spirit** (identical determinism
  mechanism, no libm) while keeping the double mandate.

## Conservative reading taken (doctrine 6)
**(B) — our own deterministic double implementations.** Rationale:
- **Fidelity.** #0014-B mandates double throughout; collapsing the seam to float
  at the very milestone where the double policy is meant to be reconciled would
  silently resolve #0014 the *opposite* way, in code, without sign-off. (B) keeps
  the double contract intact, so #0024 only *informs* #0014, it does not pre-empt
  it.
- **The determinism mechanism is the same one A3.1 proved.** A3.1 established that
  our *compiled* arithmetic (double `+ - * /`, the IEEE `sqrtsd` intrinsic) is
  bit-identical gcc-vs-clang under `-ffp-contract=off` + the pinned SSE ISA; only
  *precompiled libm .so* transcendental calls varied across machines. Our double
  polynomials are exactly that compiled-arithmetic class, so they inherit the same
  cross-compiler bit-identity — the property the cross-machine gate needs. Jolt's
  own `SinCos` is deterministic for the identical reason; we are applying the
  method, not a different one.
- **`pow`/`exp` are actually provided.** `exp(x) = 2^k·exp(r)` (Cody-Waite range
  reduction + degree-13 Taylor); `pow(b,e) = exp(e·log b)` with a deterministic
  `log` (exponent extraction + atanh series). This closes the standing #0009 note
  ("dm::pow/dm::exp deterministically backed OR the propagation refactored off
  pow") on the *back-it* branch.

### What was implemented (backing, all libm-free)
- `sin`,`cos`: quadrant range reduction + double Taylor on `[-π/4,π/4]`.
  `sin(0)==0`, `cos(0)==1` hold **bit-exactly** (M0 seam smoke assertions).
- `exp`: added to the seam as the honest base-e primitive; Cody-Waite + Taylor.
- `pow`: `exp(e·log b)`; every production caller still uses `pow(E, ·)` (base e),
  so `pow` is exercised at base e. **Call sites were NOT rerouted** to `exp` (the
  recommended-but-optional refactor) — see "Sub-fork" below.
- `sqrt`: IEEE `sqrtsd` via the SSE2 `_mm_sqrt_sd` intrinsic — correctly rounded,
  no libm symbol, no errno path. `sqrt(4)==2` and, notably, **bit-identical to the
  old libm sqrt** (the `stand` corpus hashlog did not move — it is a sqrt-only
  path).
- `abs`: sign-bit clear via `bit_cast` (IEEE-exact).
- `floor`/`ceil`: truncate-to-`long long` + adjust (deterministic; no `roundsd`
  dependency, since simcore is not compiled under the pinned SSE4.1 ISA — only
  Jolt's TUs are).
- `fmod` (unused), `tan`/`asin`/`acos`/`atan2` (unused): implemented
  deterministically so the seam compiles with **zero** libm.

### Sub-fork logged, not silently taken: reroute `pow(E,·)`→`exp`?
The orchestrator/plan recommends adding `exp` and rerouting the 13 `pow(E,·)`
sites to `dm::exp` ("removes the imprecise E literal, more honest"). I added `exp`
but **did not reroute** the call sites. Reason: A3.2's job is a *behaviour-
preserving backing swap*; keeping the call structure identical (still `pow(E,·)`,
E the full-precision Euler literal) makes the corpus regen's legitimacy trivial to
argue — the ONLY thing that changed is libm→our-poly, not the call graph — and
keeps loco/stubphys untouched (a hard constraint). The reroute is a clean, honest
follow-up (Phase A4 or a dedicated chunk) now that `exp` exists as its target.

## Accuracy achieved (max error over the used ranges, gcc == clang)
- `exp`: max **relative** error `2.2e-16` over `x∈[-3,3]` (≈ machine ε).
- `pow(E,·)`: `2.2e-13` (the double-rounding through `log(E)`, `log(E)≈1`).
- `sin`/`cos`: max **absolute** error `3.9e-13` over a full turn `[-6.5,6.5]`.
- `atan2` (unused): `2.4e-9` over `[-2,2]²`.
- Exact: `sin(0)=0`, `cos(0)=1`, `sqrt(4)=2`, `abs(-3.5)=3.5`.
This is far inside every M-test behavioural tolerance; all of M1–M7 pass on the
new backing with no assertion loosened.

## Blast radius
- **Results shift vs libm.** Every scenario whose math touches `exp`/`pow` moves
  its exact hashes (legitimate: different arithmetic). Handled by bumping
  `SIM_VERSION_TAG` `s3-stub-v1` → `a3-detmath-v1` and regenerating the M7 golden
  corpus. The `stand` hashlog did NOT move (sqrt-only), a legitimacy signal.
- **Behavioural invariants intact.** Walk ~50 m, halt terminal before `by_tick`,
  Δv small-shove absorbed ankle-only with no escalation, large shove → exactly one
  L2 escalation, M6 hash-earns-keep — all still pass. Orderings/invariants did not
  shift; only impulse-scale-free exact hashes did.
- **Seam shape.** `det_math.h` gained `exp` (declared). This is part of the S1
  surface reported ready-to-freeze in **#0025**.

## Why this is logged, not silently resolved
"Only Jolt math" cannot be met literally for a double, pow-using seam; choosing
(B) over (A) is a real fidelity fork with a persistent consequence (the whole sim
now runs on our polynomials, not libm and not Jolt-float). It **informs #0014**:
the double-vs-float reconciliation now has a concrete data point — the sim's
transcendental layer is double and deterministic without Jolt's float trig — but
this issue does **not** resolve #0014 (still human-gated). **Human-gated closure:**
confirm reading (B) (own double implementations as the S1 backing), or direct (A)
(collapse to Jolt-float, accepting the #0014-B reversal), and rule on whether the
`pow(E,·)`→`exp` reroute should be done now.

---

## RATIFIED by DayZee 2026-08-07: reading **(B)** — `det_math` backed by own inline deterministic double transcendentals (Jolt trig is float-only / no pow). The S1 surface is frozen via #0025.

# #0027 — Ambiguity: feas_L1 support-membership tolerance on real bodies (1e-9 → 1e-3)
type: ambiguity        status: closed
refs: [57] [S4] [A3] [M3]   opened: A3.4a   closed-by: signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07 (reading B)
deps: informs #0010

## What changed and why (surfaced by the A3 substitution)
`feas_L1` (loco brief §6.1, constraint 57 rung L1) tests whether the capture point
ξ lies within the L1-recoverable support region. Its terminal-capturability check
compares ξ's distance to the **support segment** (the line between the SUPPORT feet)
against a tolerance `FEAS_TOL` in `simcore/loco/wbc.cpp`. A3.4a (commit 7591b8f)
widened it: **`1e-9 m → 1e-3 m`**.

**Why the old value was an artifact, not a spec.** The throwaway analytic stub
(`StubBody`) is a *decoupled* LIPM: it holds the off-support-axis ξ component at
**exactly 0** by construction, so any tiny tolerance ("numeric noise", ~1e-9)
sufficed. That 1e-9 was never a physical threshold — it was "indistinguishable from
zero for the stub."

**Why the real body breaks it.** The Jolt articulated mech (A3.3b/A3.4) cannot null
the free (sagittal) axis to 1e-9: its quiescent `|ξ.x|` floor is ~1e-7, and a small
*absorbed* shove pushes the ξ-to-segment distance to ~1e-4. Under the old 1e-9,
`feas_L1` reported **infeasible at a clean stand** — before any disturbance — which
is physically wrong (a mech standing still is trivially L1-feasible). This is
exactly the class of hidden-stub-assumption the stub-first→substitution strategy
exists to expose.

## The interpretation question
"ξ within the reachable/recoverable support region" — measured how?
- **(A) Magic tolerance against the measure-zero segment** (current, interim):
  distance(ξ, support_segment) < `FEAS_TOL`. Widened 1e-9 → **1e-3 m**.
- **(B) Principled: ξ against the real support-POLYGON extent.** The support region
  is not a line — the box feet have a ~0.25 m half-extent, so the true support
  polygon has area. `feas_L1` should test ξ against that polygon (or an inflated
  segment of the real half-width), removing the magic constant entirely.

## Conservative reading taken (doctrine 6), and why it's inert for the stub
**(A) with `FEAS_TOL = 1e-3 m`, as an explicit interim.** Rationale:
- 1e-3 m is **1e2–1e3× inside every escalation margin** (support half-width 0.6 m;
  2-step reach 6 m), so a ξ within a millimetre of the segment is unambiguously
  1-step capturable — not escalating is the correct call.
- **Verified inert for the stub:** the committed replay corpus is **byte-identical**
  after the change (`test_m7_corpus` is the guard) and all M1–M7 behavioural tests
  stay green — so it changes **no recorded stub feas decision**. It only relaxes an
  unphysically strict bound so `feas_L1` can hold on a real body.
- Only makes `feas_L1` *more permissive* by 1e-3 vs 1e-9; both are far inside the
  region where L1 recovery is genuinely available.

## Blast radius / why logged, not silently resolved
This is a semantics change to constraint 57's L1 feasibility predicate, driven by
the real-body substitution — a doctrine-6 decision, not a tuning knob. It is logged
as its **own** ambiguity (not folded into #0018's S4-shape freeze, which is a
different concern). **Human-gated.**

**Requested action / decision points:**
1. **Ratify the interim (A)/1e-3 at the A3.6 freeze batch** (alongside #0019/#0024),
   OR
2. adopt the **principled (B)** — `feas_L1` measures ξ against the real support-
   polygon extent — landing it at **A3.4c** (ladder, where escalation ordering is
   exercised) or A4. (B) is the cleaner long-term answer; (A) is a correct,
   conservative bridge that unblocks A3.4 walking now.

## Landing note — reading (B) adopted (2026-08-07, refs #0009 #0027)
DayZee directed reading **(B)**. Landed as an ADDITIVE S4 extension (ahead of the
S4 freeze, so the complete surface freezes once — see #0018):
- **Accessor:** `IBodyState::support_half_width()` — the body's physical CoP-
  authority radius. `StubBody → 0.0` (point feet); `JoltMech → 0.25 m` (box-foot
  half-extent `kFootHalfXY`, read from the mech's own geometry).
- **`feas_L1`:** `dist(ξ, support_segment) ≤ body.support_half_width() + FEAS_EPS`,
  with `FEAS_EPS = 1e-9` a file-local NUMERIC-NOISE epsilon only. The magic
  `FEAS_TOL` (1e-9→1e-3) is **removed** from `wbc.cpp`. The single constant is now
  split into its two real meanings: (physical width) + (float noise). The separate
  `FEAS_TOL=1e-9` in `ladder.cpp` (feas_L2's terminal branch) is left untouched:
  that branch is only reached when feas_L1 already failed, so on any body it is then
  unreachable-true — out of scope here (feas_L2 reused unchanged per the workorder).

### HONEST ASSESSMENT (DayZee asked explicitly): principled + cleaner, behaviourally IDENTICAL here
The simple universe's verdict: the fix is **conceptually principled but NOT
behaviour-changing at this fidelity** — measuring ξ against the real support extent
flips **no** feas_L1 decision vs the interim 1e-3 in any current test.
- **Jolt margins (measured):** quiescent stand ξ-to-segment = **2.36e-7 m**;
  worst absorbed shove = **1.20e-4 m**. Both are ~3–6 ORDERS below BOTH the interim
  1e-3 AND the principled 0.25 — so the stand/shove are feasible under either, and
  no decision differs. Stand margin is now 0.25 − 2.36e-7 ≈ **0.25 m** (ξ sits ~1e-6×
  of the CoP-authority radius from the segment) vs the arbitrary 1e-3 before.
- **Stub:** `support_half_width = 0` ⇒ feas_L1 reduces to `d ≤ 1e-9`, i.e. EXACTLY
  the pre-A3.4a strict form. The committed replay corpus is **byte-identical**
  (test_m7_corpus green) — no recorded stub escalation decision flips (the escalation
  edge is hashed as registry id 12; it did not move). The stub never legitimately
  needs nonzero width at this fidelity: it is a decoupled LIPM on point feet holding
  off-axis ξ at machine-zero, so 0 is the physically true value.
- **What (B) actually buys over the interim (A):** it DELETES an arbitrary constant.
  The tolerance is now a REAL per-body quantity with two clean components; it reveals
  the physical truth the stub hid — **point feet have ~0 CoP authority** (L1-feasible
  only with ξ essentially AT the support), while box feet have genuine 0.25 m
  authority. It fixes the original #0027 bug (real-body stand feasible with NO magic)
  the same way (A) did, but WITHOUT a magic number. The value of doing it here is the
  cleanliness + the exposed assumption, not any changed outcome — which is exactly the
  kind of thing testing a principled approach "in this simple universe" is meant to
  reveal: at this fidelity the principled and interim forms are behaviourally
  degenerate; (B) wins on meaning, not on any decision.

**Verification:** `bash tools/ci.sh` 14/14 (incl. corpus gate + determinism lint +
gen_index --check); gcc==clang bit-identical (SHOVE 0x6c79a163888e9e9e, LADDER
0x615ec8e244e2ef5c, STAND 0x97f71cff03e77400; corpus identical under both). No
frozen seam touched; no Jolt in loco/. NOT closing — orchestrator closes on review.

---

## ORCHESTRATOR REVIEW + CLOSE (2026-08-07): reading (B) landed & verified.
Reproduced: CI 14/14, stub corpus BYTE-IDENTICAL (support_half_width=0 ⇒ feas_L1 is
the exact pre-A3.4a strict form, no stub decision flips), no frozen-seam file touched,
feas_L1 now `dist(ξ,segment) ≤ support_half_width()+FEAS_EPS` with the magic constant
removed. DayZee directed (B) and asked whether it mattered here; the honest answer
(above) is that it is behaviourally identical at this fidelity but wins on physical
meaning and removes an arbitrary number — a good use of the deterministic sandbox.
The `support_half_width()` accessor is part of the now-FROZEN S4 (#0018). CLOSED.

# #0022 — Ambiguity: feas_L2 reachable-set anchoring (plan-anchored vs stance-anchored)
type: ambiguity        status: open
refs: [57] [S5] [M4] [M5]   opened: M5 (raised in review)   closed-by: <human sign-off>
deps: defers-to PhaseB

## Source
- `loco_s3_claude_code_brief.md` §7: "`feas_L2()` predicate implemented (ξ within
  N-step reachable foothold set, N=2, analytic **union of discs**)".
- `implementation_plan_v1.2.md` constraint 57·L2: "capture point **escapes the
  planned footsteps** but **remains within the reachable foothold set** → insert
  recovery steps".

## The interpretation question
"Reachable foothold set" can be read two ways, and the two milestones implemented
it differently:
- (A) **Plan-anchored** (M4 as first shipped): union of discs around the next N=2
  *planned* footholds.
- (B) **Stance-anchored** (M5, current): a single disc of radius N·foot_reach
  around the *current stance* (kinematic reach), `foot_reach = 3.0 m` → 6.0 m.

## Why M5 moved to (B) — and why it's defensible
Under (A), the deadbeat L2 planner *places the next foothold at ξ itself*, so ξ is
always within a disc around a planned foothold → **feas_L2 can never fail**, and no
large shove would ever escalate. (B) measures against what the legs can kinematically
reach from the current support, which is what makes a genuine escape *detectable*.
Constraint 57 itself separates "escapes the **planned** footsteps" (a plan-membership
test) from "within the **reachable** foothold set" (a kinematic test) — so the
reachable set is kinematic, supporting (B). The "union of discs" phrasing collapses
to a single disc when the reachable set is modeled continuously from one stance.

## Status
M5 took reading **(B)**, documented in `issues/0006` notes; the M5 ordering test
(absorb < in-stride < escalate) passes only under a definition that *can* fail. This
is flagged here so it is visible in the ambiguity ledger rather than only in a
milestone note. **Not blocking** — it does not affect the S3 slice exit.

### Decision-point correction (2026-07-24, at #0023 sign-off — substance unchanged)
The decision point named below was **M6**, on the assumption M6 would build L2 plan
repair. It did not: M6 shipped as *hash-earns-its-keep* and closed (`8a22146`)
without touching plan repair, which belongs to **Phase B** (#0011 owns "full L2 +
recovery rungs L2–L3"). The decision point is therefore **Phase B**, recorded in
this issue's `deps:` line. This issue stays **open and human-gated**; only its
stated gate moved. Original text preserved below.

**Human-gated closure.** Natural decision point: **M6**, when L2 plan repair is built
and consumes feas_L2's semantics (repair must insert recovery steps within exactly
this reachable set). Confirm (B), or restore a plan-anchored (A) with an explicit
"escapes the planned footsteps" companion predicate.

hold:lipm-vs-rigid-trunk-pitch-drift.text:
# #0028 — Ambiguity: LIPM point-mass vs rigid-trunk pendulum — secular pitch drift in the real-body walk
type: ambiguity        status: closed
refs: [S4] [A3] [57] [44]   opened: A3.4b   closed-by: signed off by DayZee (ruling i)
deps: informs #0018; defers-to PhaseB

## What the substitution surfaced (A3.4b)
The M4 walk reproduces on the real Jolt stepping body: the SAME frozen L2
`FlatGroundStub` + L1 `Wbc` + L0 `Servo` drive a `JoltMech` that steps by ankle-
constraint management, and it walks the full 50 m M4 distance — forward progress in
the walk band (~1.84 m/s), steps landing AT the planner's footholds, planar (|y| ~
7e-4 m), feas_L2 true every tick, gcc==clang bit-identical. **But the walk is not a
clean periodic orbit: the CoM height sags MONOTONICALLY** (~5.53 m → ~5.10 m over the
50 m; the stance foot stays firmly at z=0.15 the whole time, so this is genuine trunk
FORWARD PITCH accumulating, not a contact artifact). Unremediated the pitch keeps
growing and the mech topples at ~2× the M4 distance (~100 m, ~t=1500).

## Root cause (first-principles)
The frozen controller is derived for a **Linear Inverted Pendulum**: a POINT mass at
height `h` on a MASSLESS leg, `ẍ = ω²(x − p)`, `ω = √(g/h)`. With `h = com_height() =
6`, `ω = 1.278 rad/s`. The deadbeat foot placement `p = ξ_predicted − s*` is EXACT for
that model.

The real body is NOT that model. `JoltMech`'s trunk is a **distributed rigid capsule**
(12 m, 46 t, CoM at 6 m) pivoting on the ankle point constraint. Its effective inverted-
pendulum frequency is `ω_eff² = m·g·d / I_ankle`, `I_ankle = I_cm + m·d²`. The `I_cm`
(rod-like transverse inertia of a 12 m capsule) is NOT negligible next to `m·d²`, so
`ω_eff ≈ 1.15 rad/s < ω = 1.278`. The deadbeat placement — computed with the wrong
(too-fast) ω and from a CoM the LIPM treats as a point — is therefore slightly off each
step, and the residual shows up as a slow forward-pitch mode.

Crucially, the **frozen WALKING WBC applies ZERO ankle/hip torque** (CoP pinned at the
stance foot, `tau = 0`; wbc.cpp "PASSIVE LIPM over the stance foot… foot placement is
the stabilizer, not the ankle/hip"). So there is NO trunk-pitch regulation to arrest
the mode. On the abstract stub the CoM is a point with **no orientation DOF** — "trunk
pitch" does not exist, the mode is unrepresentable, and the walk is a perfect periodic
orbit. The pitch drift is a state the real body HAS and the stub never did — the same
class of hidden-abstraction the stub→substitution strategy exists to expose (cf. #0027
feas tolerance, #0026 actuation mapping).

## The interpretation question
"Foot placement is the only walking stabilizer" (brief §7 / wbc.cpp) — is that faithful
on a real articulated body, or does the real trunk need PITCH regulation during the step?
- **(A) Accept as a documented real-body limit (interim, taken here).** The 50 m M4
  gate is met with margin; the drift is bounded and asserted non-fatal across the gate
  window. The walk is a demonstrated *positive* result at M4 scale; the secular mode is
  reported, not hidden, and left for the human/A4 to rule on. No frozen surface touched.
- **(B) Add trunk-pitch regulation to the WALKING branch** — a small ankle/hip torque
  keeping trunk pitch near vertical DURING the step (not just foot placement). This is a
  change to the FROZEN L1 `Wbc` walking law (S-frozen) — must NOT be done under A3.4b;
  it is a controller-design decision for the human (and would also inform whether the
  LIPM abstraction is adequate for the melee bodies at all).
- **(C) Match the model to the body:** feed the controller the real effective pendulum
  height `h_eff = g/ω_eff²` so its ω matches reality. But `com_height` is entangled with
  the physical geometry (it sets the trunk's placement height, which changes `d`, which
  changes `ω_eff` — circular), so this is not a clean single knob and risks looking like
  a tuned-to-pass number. Rejected as an A3.4b self-fix.

## Conservative reading taken (doctrine 6)
**(A).** Rationale:
- The workorder's own instruction: "a partial honest result + a clear fork beats a
  forced number." The 50 m M4 ordering/behavioural invariants HOLD (forward progress,
  band, foothold tracking, feas_L2, planarity, no fall, determinism). Only the *magnitude*
  of long-horizon stability differs from the stub's perfect orbit — sanctioned to shift
  (kickoff §2), and here reported quantitatively rather than tuned away.
- (B) touches a frozen seam and is a genuine control-design fork; (C) is not a clean knob
  and would be exactly the "tune until the number passes" move the workorder forbids.

## Blast radius / why logged
This is the load-bearing honesty finding of A3.4b. It bears on **#0018 (S4 freeze)**: the
S4 read/actuation SHAPE is unchanged and honoured by the second implementation, but the
substitution shows the LIPM controller the seam feeds is only APPROXIMATELY right for a
distributed rigid body over long horizons — a fact that should be on the record before
S4 freezes and before the melee bodies (constraint 44) lean on the same walk law. It does
NOT change the seam, does NOT close #0018, and touches no frozen surface. **Human-gated:**
ratify (A) as the A3.4 interim, or direct (B) trunk-pitch regulation (a frozen-L1 change)
/ another remedy, and rule whether the LIPM walk law is adequate for the melee scale or
needs a distributed-inertia correction.

---

## DECIDED by DayZee Christopher Reay, 2026-08-07: reading (B).
Direct the walk law to **turn on the angular-momentum channel** — regulate trunk
pitch during the step, not foot-placement-only. The rationale is architectural, not
merely a drift fix: this is the balance floor acquiring the one faculty (whole-body
angular momentum) that every future striking/skill controller must borrow from — it
is rung zero of the movement-control architecture proposed in **#0029**. The stub's
CoM is a point with no orientation, so the regulation must be formulated to be
inert-or-legitimate on the point-mass stub (candidate: regulate the CoM's horizontal
offset from the support geometry — derivable from existing `IBodyState` `com_pos` +
`support_segment`, ~0 on the stub's steady walk, non-zero as the real trunk pitches —
so no S4 seam extension is needed). Note: the WBC walk law is internal L1 logic, NOT
a frozen seam (S2/S3/S5/S6 untouched). Implementation delegated as the next A3 chunk
(refs #0028). **This issue stays OPEN until that chunk lands and the drift is verified
eliminated** (CoM height bounded over the full walk and well beyond), whereupon it
closes on evidence.

---

## A3.4b-B evidence (implementation landed; issue STAYS OPEN for human review)
The angular-momentum channel is turned ON in the L1 walking branch (`loco/wbc.cpp`):
two bounded secondary terms, foot placement stays primary.
- **(1) ankle-CoP CoM-offset regulation** (the directed formulation): `dp = clamp(
  -k_p·off, patch)`, `off` = CoM along-travel offset from the support midpoint,
  `patch = 0.25 m` (the box-foot half-extent; the seam under-reports the support as
  the ankle point), `k_p = 1`. Emitted through the CoP channel.
- **(2) hip-flywheel momentum shed**: `tau = -k_L·ang_momentum()`, `k_L = 0.02`.

**Stub inertness / corpus.** Not byte-identical, but dynamics-inert: `StubBody`
re-clamps any commanded CoP to its single-support POINT, so the stub CoM trajectory
is byte-identical (M4 final CoM x = 44.810034911838549 with and without the change,
to 1e-15) and the hip term is identically 0 (stub `ell ≡ 0`). Only the *recorded CoP
setpoint payload* changed, so the golden corpus was legitimately regen'd (tag bump
`a3-detmath-v1 → a3-0028-walkreg-v2`). `stand.hashlog` is unchanged (standing branch
untouched); every M-suite behavioural invariant is preserved *by construction* (the
trajectory is unchanged) and all M0–M7 tests are green. gcc==clang bit-identical
(`A3_WALK_HASH=0x8213720108b049d6`; corpus identical under both).

**Result on the Jolt body.** The drift is REDUCED: CoM-height min over 50 m rises
~5.07→5.15; over ~1500 ticks (2× M4) it stays bounded at min ≈ 4.75 (vs baseline
~4.72 then collapse at ~t1547). `test_a3_jolt_walk` block (a2) asserts this.

**HONEST LIMIT — the drift is only SLOWED, not eliminated (for human ruling).**
First-principles finding surfaced while implementing: the real long-horizon failure
is not a gentle pitch but a rigid-trunk forward **somersault**. Because the single
capsule is BOTH trunk and pendulum, the LIPM vault rotates it ~0.16 rad forward each
step and the foot-switch never resets its *absolute* orientation, so it must rotate
through inversion; the CoM secularly sags and the constraint solver then diverges
(~t1560, ~101 m). This is **independent of the start IC** (verified: seeding the
exact LIPM orbit — trunk leaned back by c0 with the orbit ω — still collapses at
t1556) and **cannot be arrested by bounded reactive torque**: resetting the per-step
rotation needs ~9e5 N·m, versus the servo's Q13-placeholder hip budget
(`torque_k·volume = 8e4 N·m`) and even full-weight bounded CoP authority (`W·0.25 ≈
1.1e5`). Empirically no bounded law (hip-shed, ankle-CoP, com_vel/ang-momentum rate,
either sign, any combination) moves the collapse more than ~30 ticks / ~1 m; the
present regulation is the best honest reduction found. NOTE also: the DECISION's
premise that the CoM offset from support is "~0 on the stub's steady walk" is
empirically FALSE — the stub vaults ±0.4 m (mean +0.035), essentially like the real
body; the only signals identically zero on the stub are `ang_momentum`, `com_vel().z`
and `com_pos().z − h`. **Fork for the human:** reading (B) alone is necessary but
insufficient at this actuation authority — full remediation appears to need reading
(C) (model-match ω/h_eff), a larger actuation budget (the Q13 hip law is a
placeholder), or an articulated body where the trunk is not the pendulum. Bears on
whether the LIPM walk law is adequate for the melee bodies (#0018 / constraint 44).

---

## ORCHESTRATOR REVIEW (2026-08-07): (B) verified & ACCEPTED; issue STAYS OPEN
Reproduced independently: CI 12/12; `A3_WALK_HASH=0x8213720108b049d6` bit-identical
gcc-vs-clang with identical WALK/LONG/HALT traces; the regen'd corpus reproduces the
committed goldens byte-for-byte under BOTH compilers; the two regulators are provably
inert on the stub dynamics (CoP re-clamped to the support point, stub hip momentum ≡ 0)
so the corpus change is a pure setpoint-payload regen and every M-suite behavioural
invariant holds. (B) is a legitimate, deterministic improvement and the balance floor
now has its first angular-momentum faculty (rung zero of #0029) — that architectural
goal is achieved regardless of the drift.

**But #0028's close criterion ("drift verified ELIMINATED") is NOT met — the drift is
only slowed. Issue stays OPEN.** The reason is now understood and it is LARGER than a
control-law tuning: the A3.3b mech is a SINGLE capsule that is simultaneously trunk and
pendulum, with no articulation to keep the trunk upright while the legs swing. So each
LIPM vault rotates the whole rigid body and nothing resets its absolute orientation —
an intrinsic, IC-independent somersault that bounded reactive torque at the Q13-
placeholder authority cannot arrest (the honest note above quantifies it). The 50 m M4
substitution GATE is met and deterministic; the collapse is at ~101 m (2× M4), beyond
A3's remit but squarely relevant to sustained locomotion and the melee bodies.

**This escalates the fork from "which walk-law reading" to a MECH-MODEL / MORPHOLOGY
decision** — the most consequential of the (C) / bigger-actuation / **articulated-legs**
options is articulation (a proper walker decouples the trunk from leg-swing). That is
genuinely bigger than A3 (it reshapes the mech body plan; cf. charter §4, constraint 44,
the movement-control floor in #0029) and is surfaced to the human rather than decided.
A3 continues on the M4-gate-met walk; short-horizon A3.4c work (ladder, hash-earns-keep)
is unaffected by the long-horizon somersault. **Human ruling requested** on whether to
(i) accept (B) as the A3 walk and route the articulation/actuation remedy to Phase-B
melee-body work, or (ii) redesign the mech toward articulated legs before proceeding.

---

## RULING by DayZee Christopher Reay, 2026-08-07: (i) — CLOSED.
Accept (B) — the angular-momentum walk regulator (commit 06321bb) — as the A3 walk.
The M4 50 m gate is met and deterministic; that is sufficient for A3's "substitute
Jolt, re-run the A2 suite" remit. The deeper remedy for sustained locomotion —
**articulated legs** (a mech body plan where the trunk is decoupled from leg-swing so
it stays upright), and/or a real (non-placeholder-Q13) actuation budget — is **routed
to Phase-B melee-body work** (`defers-to PhaseB`, #0011), where the multi-segment
combat mechs are built. This closes the "which walk-law reading" question; the
morphology work it points to lives in Phase B, informed by the movement-control floor
in #0029 and constraint 44. Rung zero (#0029's angular-momentum floor) is banked.

# #0019 — Ambiguity: ω = √(g/h) — gravity source for the controller (S4 read surface)
type: ambiguity        status: closed
refs: [S4] [45] [57]   opened: M3   closed-by: signed off by DayZee 2026-08-07
deps: defers-to A3; informs #0018

## Constraint / source
- The L1 controller and `feas_L1` need the LIPM natural frequency `ω = √(g/h)`
  (loco brief §6.1; units charter §1 fixes g = 9.81 m/s², scenario-overridable).
- The S4 read surface (`IBodyState`, `simcore/stubphys/body.h`) exposes
  `com_height()` (h) and `mass()`, but **NOT** gravity and **NOT** ω. `BodyParams`
  carries `gravity` but `BodyParams` is not part of the read seam.
- So a consumer holding only an `IBodyState&` cannot read g; it must obtain ω from
  somewhere else. `feas_L1`'s mandated signature is `(IBodyState, PreviewWindow)`
  only [57a] — it cannot even take a params argument.

## The two readings
- (A) g is a **charter-global constant** the controller may reconstruct ω from
  (a code/data constant equal to 9.81), because at this fidelity every body shares
  the charter g and `BodyParams.gravity` merely echoes it.
- (B) g/ω is **per-body world data** that belongs on the read surface — S4 gains a
  `gravity()` (or `omega()`) accessor so a controller reads the body's actual g,
  honouring the charter's "scenario-overridable" note for low-g levels.

## Conservative reading taken (doctrine 6)
**(A) — reconstruct ω from the charter constant g.** In the WBC it lives as hashed
mech data (`WbcParams.gravity = 9.81`, so a low-g scenario is expressible by
per-mech config today); in `feas_L1` (which takes no params by mandate) it is a
file-scope constant `FEAS_GRAVITY = 9.81`. Both equal `BodyParams.gravity`'s
default, so every consumer agrees and M3 is bit-consistent. Rationale: adding a
`gravity()`/`omega()` method would MODIFY the S4 seam at the very milestone we are
reporting it ready-to-freeze (#0018), and the brief says avoid modifying
`stubphys/` and grow no interface speculatively. Reading (A) needs no seam change.

## Blast radius
Cosmetic today (all g = 9.81). It bites only if a scenario sets a body's gravity
away from the charter default AND a controller must see it: then `feas_L1` would
compute ω from 9.81 while the body integrates with the scenario g — a mismatch.
The clean fix at that point is reading (B) (add `gravity()`/`omega()` to S4).

## Why this is logged, not silently resolved
The natural decision point is the **S4 freeze at A3** (the Jolt body makes the
gravity source concrete). Pinning it now keeps the freeze (#0018) honest: the seam
is frozen with this question explicitly answered rather than resolved by accident
in controller code. **Human-gated closure**: confirm reading (A), or amend to (B)
with the accessor added to `IBodyState` at/ before the A3 freeze.

---

## RATIFIED by DayZee 2026-08-07: reading **(A)** — ω reconstructed from the charter constant g (no gravity accessor on S4). Per-scenario gravity, if ever needed, is a future additive S4 amendment.
