# #0030 — S7 ready to freeze: command bus / `PlanIntent` + the true delay pipeline
type: freeze-request        status: open
refs: [S7] [A4] [9] [49]   opened: A4   closed-by: <human sign-off>
deps: informs #0010

Per the kickoff seam table, S7 (`command bus / PlanIntent`, `test-inject → delay
pipeline`) is scheduled to **FREEZE at A4**. A4.1 (parent #0010) builds the seam;
reporting **ready to freeze** — not freezing unilaterally (doctrine 8: freezing
itself requires sign-off).

This replaces the A2/A3 direct `PlanIntent` injection (the sanctioned temporary
shortcut, kickoff §2): outside input now flows through the bus, delayed by class.

## The delay law (charter §2 — exact integers, not this seam's to change)
| Class | Delay | Charter | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CONSCIOUS` | **9 ticks (300 ms)** | D  | pilot `PlanIntent` |
| `SCRIPT`    | **3 ticks (100 ms)** | Ds | scripted / subconscious action (A4.4 exercises it) |
| `IMMEDIATE` | **0 ticks**          | —  | a SHOVE — a physical DISTURBANCE, not a command |

A command ISSUED at tick T takes effect at exactly `T + delay(class)`. A SHOVE is
the world acting on the mech, so it is immediate; only pilot/script INTENT is
delayed — the pilot's *reaction* is what is 300 ms stale, never the world's action.
The constructor's initial `PlanIntent` is START STATE (in effect at t=0, NOT
delayed); only mid-run intent CHANGES traverse the pipeline.

## Frozen surface (proposed)
```cpp
// simcore/loco/command_bus.{h,cpp}  — Jolt-free (loco/ + stubphys/ only)
enum class DelayClass : uint8_t { IMMEDIATE = 0, SCRIPT = 1, CONSCIOUS = 2 };
constexpr uint64_t delay_ticks(DelayClass);   // → {0, 3, 9}  (charter §2)

struct BusCommand {                           // an in-flight command (hashable)
    enum class Kind : uint8_t { PLAN_INTENT = 0, SHOVE = 1 };
    Kind kind; DelayClass klass;
    uint64_t issue_tick, effective_tick;      // effective = issue + delay(klass)
    PlanIntent intent; Shove shove;           // one valid per kind (both hashed)
    void hash_into(Hasher&) const;
};

class CommandBus : public IHashable {         // the pending queue IS world state
    void issue_intent(uint64_t issue_tick, const PlanIntent&, DelayClass = CONSCIOUS);
    void issue_shove (uint64_t issue_tick, const Shove&,      DelayClass = IMMEDIATE);
    std::vector<BusCommand> release_due(uint64_t now);   // canonical order
    void hash_into(Hasher&) const override;              // count + queue, in order
};
```

## Determinism contract (part of the seam)
- The in-flight (pending) queue is **WORLD STATE** → `CommandBus` is `IHashable`
  and is registered in each world's `HashRegistry` (WalkWorld id 13, LocoWorld
  id 8), so a **held/in-flight command shows in the per-tick hash** [49].
- Canonical order: `(effective_tick, kind, issue_seq)`; within a tick a SHOVE
  releases before an intent (matching the pre-A4 apply order). The queue is kept
  sorted so both the release order and the digest are issue-order-independent.
- The bus is world state; the **input schedule (what the pilot issues, at its
  ISSUE tick) is NOT hashed** — it is the replay INPUT, analogous to
  `ReplayFile.commands`. This keeps the queue empty (and the hash unpolluted)
  until a command is actually issued.

## Evidence (green conformance)
- `simcore/loco/command_bus.{h,cpp}`: the seam (one real implementation; the bus
  is the substitution point that replaced direct injection — the seam earns its
  existence, doctrine 8).
- `test_a4_command_bus` (new gate) passing:
  - the timing law at the bus: a command issued at T=100 releases at exactly
    **109 (CONSCIOUS)**, **103 (SCRIPT)**, **100 (IMMEDIATE)**;
  - canonical intra-tick order (a co-effective shove releases before an intent);
  - the held command changes the bus digest and draining restores the empty
    digest (a held command is visible in the hash) [49];
  - **WalkWorld end-to-end**: a HALT issued at tick 100 flips `intent()` at
    **exactly tick 109** (CONSCIOUS) / **103** (SCRIPT); a shove lands at its
    issue tick (delay 0);
  - "held command earns its hash": two WalkWorlds, one with an intent in flight,
    are body/controller byte-coincident during ticks 100–108 yet their tick
    hashes DIFFER (the divergence is the held command) — and are EQUAL before the
    issue tick (the inbox is input, not state).
- `test_m7_corpus` (the CI regression gate) passing on the regenerated corpus
  (`SIM_VERSION_TAG a3-0028-walkreg-v2 → a4-0010-cmdbus-delay-v1`). The command
  streams (`.replay`) are UNCHANGED bit-for-bit except the tag (records at ISSUE
  tick). Every behavioural invariant holds: walk 50 m; **walk-halt** reaches the
  Remain terminal at rest with 0 escalations (the halt, issued at tick 90, now
  takes effect 9 ticks later at tick 99 — halt-as-plan, just later); shove-absorb
  ≤ L1 (0 escalations, walks on); shove-escalate → exactly 1 layer-2 escalation.
- `gcc == clang` bit-identical corpus (single-machine cross-compiler proxy) — see
  the A4.1 report.

## Scope note
The A4.4 Jolt exit test wires the SAME bus into the Jolt walk world (the 100 ms
scripted reaction + the 300 ms pilot pipeline on the real body). A4.1 delivers the
seam and proves it on the stub worlds (the corpus + `WalkWorld`); the Jolt world
(`phys/jolt_walk_world.h`, an internal A3 test harness, not a corpus world) still
uses direct injection and is re-wired by A4.4, behind this same frozen surface.

## Requested action
Human sign-off to mark **S7 FROZEN**. After sign-off, changes to the command-bus
interface / the delay classes require a logged plan amendment. The delay integers
(9 / 3 / 0 ticks) are charter §2 and are not this seam's to change.

---

## ⚠ HOLD — do NOT freeze S7 as-is (Rev 2 / #0032), 2026-08-07
The command-bus MECHANISM survives (queue, effective-tick, hashed), but its delay model
changes (fixed 9/3 classes → H+R config) and the bus now also carries **script layer setpoint
outputs**, not just PlanIntent. S7's surface is revised BEFORE any freeze. This freeze-
request is paused pending the Rev-2 S7 redesign.

---

## Rev-2 S7 surface — adoption step 1 done (refs #0032 §2/§3, #0010), 2026-08-08 — STILL OPEN / ON HOLD
Adoption step 1 (the S7 Rev-2 command vocabulary) is IMPLEMENTED in
`simcore/loco/command_bus.{h,cpp}` — behaviour-preserving (stub corpus byte-identical,
`test_m7_corpus` green, gcc==clang). The bus MECHANISM is unchanged (canonical-order
in-flight queue, effective-tick, `IHashable`, registered id 8/13); only the VOCABULARY
moved. This is NOT a freeze — the surface is not final until script layer v0 lands (step 2),
so this freeze-request stays OPEN and ON HOLD. The revised surface:

| Kind / class | delay | payload | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DelayClass::PILOT_HOLD` (=2) | **H** ticks, `kDefaultHoldH` **config**, default 9 | `PlanIntent` | pilot intent, HELD H ticks at the server. Retires the fixed `CONSCIOUS=9`/"300 ms" class — no charter-pinned conscious delay; engine knows only ticks. Default 9 preserves walk-halt timing. |
| `Kind::SERVO_SETPOINT` (=2) | **0** (IMMEDIATE) | `PlanIntent` (reused) | Rev 2 §3: the realtime script layer streams setpoints LIVE. `CommandBus::inject_script layer_setpoint(tick, setpoint)` installs the live-inject path; drains same-tick (never lingers in the hashed queue), mirroring an IMMEDIATE shove. **NOTHING emits it yet** — script layer v0 (step 2) plugs in here. |
| `DelayClass::IMMEDIATE` (=0) | **0** | `Shove` | a SHOVE — a physical DISTURBANCE, unchanged. |
| `DelayClass::SCRIPT` (=1) | 3 ticks | `PlanIntent` | **KEPT, superseded-pending-script layer.** The A4.2 tree's `open_script_claim` still issues through it; Rev 2 has no fixed Ds. Removed when the tree's script principal → script layer (step 2). |

- **Enum values are stable** (they are hashed via `BusCommand`): PILOT_HOLD re-casts the
  old CONSCIOUS value 2 as the config-H server-hold — a re-framing, not a renumber — so the
  corpus is byte-identical. SERVO_SETPOINT reuses the `intent` payload field, so
  `BusCommand::hash_into` is byte-identical (no new hashed field).
- **H vs R (documented, not built):** H (server-hold) is the sim-core-execution delay —
  the server executes a pilot intent at T+H, and H lives in this seam. **R (apply-at-replica)
  is the REPLICATION/REPLAY-LAYER offset** — how far behind a deterministic replica replays
  the executed stream — and is NOT a sim-core-execution parameter; nothing in `command_bus`
  consumes R. It is recorded in the header only so R is not confused with H. No replica built.
- **Still to land before any freeze (step 2, script layer):** the final SERVO_SETPOINT payload
  schema (currently reuses `PlanIntent`); the pilot-intent-vs-live-setpoint arbitration
  order in the tree; retiring SCRIPT once the tree's script principal is script layer-hosted.

---

## ⚠ SUPERSEDED IN FRAMING by the Rev-2 bus spec #0033, 2026-08-08
S7 is now 'the mech bus' — a permissioned channel pub/sub fabric (#0033), of which
the current `command_bus` PlanIntent/setpoint/shove is the minimal subset. The
ACTUATOR channels are the recorded deterministic stream; sensor/goal channels feed
the script layer and are not recorded. S7 stays OPEN/HOLD — it freezes only once the bus
reflects #0033 (built via script layer v0).

---

## RE-HOMED TO PHASE B at the Phase-A close (DayZee, 2026-08-09) — S7 NOT frozen now.
At the Phase-A close batch, S7 was considered for freezing and DELIBERATELY NOT FROZEN.
The record forbids it: #0032 says "do NOT freeze S7 as-is — its surface is revised first,"
and this issue is stamped ON HOLD until "the bus reflects #0033 (built via script layer v0)."
That full-channel bus (#0033 §6 / A4.1's deferred half) was not built in Phase A, so the S7
surface is explicitly non-final. Freezing it now would freeze a surface the record calls
provisional — the exact seam-hygiene error freezing exists to prevent.

**S7's freeze therefore moves into Phase B: it freezes once the #0033 full-channel bus lands
there.** This issue STAYS OPEN as the standing S7 freeze-request; the ready-to-freeze
condition is now "the first-class SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL channels exist." This is
consistent with the Phase-B frozen-seam-amendment authorization recorded in #0011 /
ARCHITECTURE.md §4.

# #0006 — M5: recovery ladder rungs L0–L1
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M5] [57]   opened: M5   closed-by: aca6203

M5 deliverable (loco brief §9, §11): the bottom two rungs of the recovery ladder.
A mech absorbs a mid-stride shove without escalating past L1; a large shove
escalates exactly once.

## Tests
- [x] Mid-stride impulse Δv = 0.15 m/s → absorbed via step-timing adjustment, plan intact, no escalation past L1 [57·L1].
- [x] Large impulse (tuned Δv = 10.0 m/s) → `feas_L2` fails → exactly one `EscalationReason{layer=2}` recorded.
- [x] Ladder predicate signatures take (IBodyState, PreviewWindow) only — source-agnostic by signature [57a].
- [x] Ordering invariant holds: absorb < in-stride < escalate.

## Notes

### What was built (bottom two rungs + escalation RECORDING, not consumption)
- `simcore/loco/ladder.{h,cpp}`: `ladder_eval(IBodyState, PreviewWindow) -> LadderResult`,
  the per-tick BOTTOM-UP evaluation run AFTER L1. feas_L1 → feas_L2, stop at first
  failure. Semantics: feas_L1 holds ⇒ L0/L1 absorb (no escalation); feas_L1 fails but
  feas_L2 holds ⇒ L1 in-stride catches it in-plan (no escalation); feas_L2 fails ⇒
  RECORD `EscalationReason{layer=2}` (L2 plan repair is NOT built — that is M6).
- `feas_L2` redefined stance-anchored: ξ is 2-step reachable iff within N·foot_reach
  (= 2·3.0 = 6.0 m) of the CURRENT stance. Anchoring to the body (not to the already-
  deadbeat-replanned preview footholds) is what makes an un-catchable shove DETECTABLE
  — the planner chases ξ with placement but not beyond kinematic reach.
- `simcore/loco/wbc.cpp`: the L1 in-stride step-timing law made ACTIVE. Closed form,
  no tolerance loop, no current-tick input (signature-clean). resid = (ξ − ξ_prop)·d̂,
  ξ_prop = p + (ξ_prev − p)·e^{ω·DT} (exact single-support LIPM flow); on the periodic
  orbit resid ≈ 0 (inside a deadband ⇒ retime 0 ⇒ steady walk untouched), a shove spikes
  it. Quantized through a deadband and CLAMPED to ±2 ticks; a forward shove ⇒ touch down
  earlier (advance, −retime). Gated off on the touchdown-tick stance switch. GaitFsm gains
  `prev_stance` + `warm` (hashed).
- `simcore/loco/stepper.cpp`: footholds CLAMPED to `foot_reach` of the foot they step
  from (`clamp_to_reach`). Feet cannot teleport — inactive on the steady gait (stride
  0.9 m << reach 3.0 m; M4 unchanged) and active only when a disturbance throws the
  deadbeat target beyond reach. This makes feas_L2 meaningful (placement cannot chase a
  ξ that escaped the reachable set) and makes a large-shove escape SUSTAINED (one onset,
  not a fail/recover/fail oscillation).
- `simcore/loco/loco_world.h` (WalkWorld): the escalation stream — a hashable
  `std::vector<EscalationReason>` registered at id 12 (with its edge-trigger state); the
  ±2-tick retime applied to `frame_.next_touchdown` once per step (id 11 gains the latch).
  Escalations recorded on the RISING EDGE of infeasibility (one structured reason per
  onset). No handler above L2 exists — recorded, not consumed [S8 PROVISIONAL].

### Source-agnostic signatures (verbatim, no cause parameter)
    bool         feas_L1(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
    bool         feas_L2(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
    LadderResult ladder_eval(const IBodyState&, const PreviewWindow&);
Asserted at compile time in test_m5 via exact function-pointer types.

### Tuned magnitudes + capturability numbers (ω = √(9.81/6.0) = 1.2782)
Stub landmarks: ankle half-width 0.6 m (L0); 2-step reachable radius N·foot_reach =
2·3.0 = 6.0 m (feas_L2).
- absorb   Δv = 0.05 (M3): ξ excursion 0.05/ω = 0.039 m  < 0.6  → L0 ankle absorbs.
- in-stride Δv = 0.15     : ξ excursion 0.117 m; feas_L1 marginal (fails 141× post-shove),
                            feas_L2 holds; step-timing engaged (retime −2 at the shove
                            tick); 0 escalations; mech walked on to x = 17.5 m. (brief
                            value, KEPT.)
- escalate  Δv = 10.0     : ξ excursion 7.82 m > 6.0 m — escapes the 2-step reach. Exactly
                            ONE layer-2 escalation, verified robust across shove ticks
                            30–44 and windows 200/400/900. TUNED UP from the brief's 0.6
                            (excursion 0.47 m — trivially in-stride for this 50-ton, 6 m,
                            3 m-reach stub) per brief §11 ("tune to the stub's actual
                            capturability numbers; preserve the ordering"). Ordering in
                            ξ-excursion: 0.039 < 0.117 < 7.82; against landmarks 0.039 <
                            0.6 and 7.82 > 6.0.

### Escalation counts asserted
- test (a) in-stride: 0 escalations (layer ≥ 2 count = 0).
- test (b) escalate : exactly 1, {layer=2, predicate_id=feas_L2, budget=6.0, margin<0}.

### Determinism
Escalation buffer + edge state + retime latch all hash_into (registered ids 11/12); the
large-shove scenario replays bit-identically (test b-det). No `float`, transcendentals via
det_math (dm::pow(E,·)), all timing integer-tick, fixed-iteration. M0–M4 unchanged.

# #0007 — M6: hash-earns-its-keep (firmware state is load-bearing)
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M6] [3] [49]   opened: M6   closed-by: 8a22146

M6 deliverable (loco brief §11): prove `[49]` is load-bearing — that controller
state inside the hash catches divergence a physics-only hash would miss.

## Tests
- [x] Construct two runs whose physics states coincide at tick T but whose `GaitFsm` differs → assert tick hashes differ at T.
- [x] If the test cannot be constructed, document why in the test file. (N/A — the dynamic construction WAS achievable; see Notes.)

## Notes (M6 delivered — `simcore/tests/test_m6_hash.cpp`)

**Construction (dynamic, bit-reproducible).** Two identical `LocoWorld` stands on a
`Remain` terminal (the M3 stand: feet on ±Y, CoM offset 0.05 m). Run B's controller
is perturbed mid-stand via the new `LocoWorld::fsm_mut()` test hook.

**Perturbed field: `GaitFsm::phase_t`** (the gait dwell clock), `+= 0.5 s` injected
just before tick 50; observed at **T = 120**.

**Why physics stays bit-identical (⇒ physics-only hash matches).** The emitted
`CopCommand`/`SplineSet` is a pure function of (body state, preview, `WbcParams`).
In `Wbc::wbc_step`, `phase_t` is ONLY WRITTEN — the single line
`fsm.phase_t = fsm.phase_t + DT` — and is NEVER READ to compute the CoP, the hip
torque, or the ±2-tick step-timing (that block is gated `!preview.is_terminal()` and
reads `prev_xi/prev_stance/warm`, never `phase_t`). So the offset never enters the
setpoints ⇒ both bodies integrate identical commands each substep ⇒ physics is
bit-for-bit identical. Because `phase_t` merely accumulates (+DT/tick), the injected
offset PERSISTS unchanged to T (chosen over `step_retime`, which is inert on a Remain
terminal but is recomputed to 0 each tick, so it would not survive to a later T). This
is exactly the [49] case: a diverged controller state that HAS NOT YET acted on the body.

**Result (registry ids: id 2 = body dyn state = PHYSICS; id 5 = `GaitFsm` = CONTROLLER).**
- FULL tick hash at T=120 — **DIFFER**: A=`0x39bdd4ae0962c275`, B=`0x3deb41c3e57ba881`.
- PHYSICS-ONLY hash at T=120 — **MATCH**: A=B=`0x760125dc0e6e4ea2`
  (`LocoWorld::physics_only_hash()` folds body config id 1 + body state id 2, excluding
  the `GaitFsm`). This proves that WITHOUT folding the `GaitFsm` the divergence would
  pass silently — i.e. [49] is load-bearing.
- The property is asserted at every tick from injection to T, not only at T. A unit-level
  lemma over `HashRegistry` (identical body + differing `GaitFsm`) corroborates it.

**Test hooks added to `simcore/loco/loco_world.h`** (test-support, not a seam; hashed
state unaffected): `GaitFsm& fsm_mut()` (inject the controller-only divergence) and
`uint64_t physics_only_hash() const` (the physics-only contrast digest).

# #0008 — M7: replay corpus + CI regression
type: milestone        status: closed
refs: [M7] [3] [4]   opened: M7   closed-by: 4f452dc

M7 deliverable (loco brief §10, §11): the committed replay corpus and the CI
regression primitive (re-run corpus, diff hash logs). Closes the Phase A A2
stub-first locomotion slice (M0–M7).

## Tests
- [x] Replay corpus committed: stand / walk-halt / shove-absorb / shove-escalate.
- [x] CI job re-runs the corpus and fails on any hash-log mismatch.
- [x] Replay file format = {scenario id, seed, version tag, command stream}; per-tick hash log alongside.

## What landed
- `simcore/replay/replay.{h,cpp}` — the replay-file format + `serialize_replay`/
  `parse_replay` (deterministic, human-diffable, byte-stable round-trip: fixed
  field order, `%.17g` lossless floats), plus the pinned version tags.
- `simcore/replay/scenarios.{h,cpp}` — the INTERNAL scenario registry (not a
  seam; a small explicit 4-entry table per kickoff doctrine 2, NOT a generic
  engine) + `record`/`replay`.
- `simcore/tests/test_m7_corpus.cpp` — THE CI regression gate (runs under ctest
  → tools/ci.sh).
- `tools/record_corpus.cpp` — the REGEN path (executable target `record_corpus`).
- `corpus/` (repo root) — committed `<id>.replay` (inputs) + `<id>.hashlog`
  (golden per-tick hash log) for each of the 4 scenarios.

## Notes

### Replay file format (`ReplayFile`)
`{ uint32 format_version; string scenario_id; uint64 seed; string sim_version_tag;
vector<Command> commands }` where `Command = { uint64 tick; Kind{PLAN_INTENT,
SHOVE}; PlanIntent intent; Shove shove }`. `kReplayFormatVersion = 1`.
`SIM_VERSION_TAG = "s3-stub-v1"` — pinned in one header (`replay.h`); a deliberate
sim change that legitimately moves the goldens must bump it (the tag rides in
every replay file, so a stale corpus is self-identifying). `seed` is carried but
UNUSED: there is no RNG in S3 — it is pinned for format forward-compatibility
(constraint [3]), never a branch on sim logic. The S7 command-bus / 300 ms delay
pipeline is Phase A4 (brief §12): in S3 each command is applied UNDELAYED at its
stated tick.

On-disk layout (line-oriented, labelled tokens for diffability):
```
format_version 1
scenario_id walk-halt
seed 0
sim_version_tag s3-stub-v1
command_count 1
command 90 PLAN_INTENT kind HALT vel 0 0 0 halt 11.199999999999999 0 0 stance 0 by_tick 210
```

### The 4 scenarios (each lifts a known-good milestone setup; the initial stance
+ initial intent are baked into the builder keyed by scenario_id — the command
stream carries only the mid-run PlanIntent/Shove commands):
- `stand` (1800 ticks, M3 a): LocoWorld on a Remain plan, feet on the Y support
  axis (±0.6 m), 5 cm CoM offset. No commands. Behaviour: the offset is nulled
  (final |com_y| < 1e-3).
- `walk-halt` (400 ticks, M4): WalkWorld cruise 3 m/s on the periodic orbit; one
  command — PLAN_INTENT halt-at (x=11.2 by tick 210) at tick 90. Behaviour:
  decelerates to the Remain terminal, at rest (|vx| < 1e-2), no escalation.
- `shove-absorb` (300 ticks, M5 a): WalkWorld walk 1.8 m/s; one SHOVE Δv=0.15 m/s
  (7500 N·s +X) at tick 37. Behaviour: absorbed in-stride, ZERO layer-2
  escalations, keeps walking (final x > 10 m).
- `shove-escalate` (400 ticks, M5 b): WalkWorld walk 1.8 m/s; one SHOVE Δv=10 m/s
  (500000 N·s +X) at tick 37. Behaviour: ξ escapes the 2-step reach → feas_L2
  fails → EXACTLY ONE layer-2 escalation.

### Where the corpus lives
`corpus/` at the repo root (8 files: `<id>.replay` + `<id>.hashlog` ×4). The path
is compiled into the test and the regen tool via `MK_CORPUS_DIR`
(`${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/corpus`) so it resolves from any build dir (incl. a fresh
`rm -rf build`).

### Regen command (only on an INTENDED sim change; bump SIM_VERSION_TAG then)
```
cmake --build build --target record_corpus && ./build/simcore/record_corpus
```

### How the gate fails
`test_m7_corpus` parses each `.replay`, `replay()`s it, and `diff_logs` against
the golden `.hashlog`; a mismatch is a build break and prints the FIRST DIVERGING
TICK (the hash-diff bisector's atom). It also asserts the replay text round-trips
byte-exactly, the `sim_version_tag` matches, and each scenario's known behaviour
still holds (e.g. shove-escalate records exactly one layer-2 escalation) so the
corpus is meaningful, not merely self-consistent. This realises the A1/M0 "CI job
that replays the corpus" requirement now that there is real content.

### S3 slice status against constraint numbers (kickoff §5/§13 report)
The A2 stub-first locomotion slice (M0–M7) satisfies, at STUB fidelity:
- [1] fixed 30 Hz lockstep tick + [2] 120 Hz physics substeps — `core/tick.h`, held across every milestone.
- [3] state hash + versioned replay file — M0 hasher/registry; M7 full replay-file format + `SIM_VERSION_TAG`/`format_version`.
- [4] headless CI replay corpus hash-matches every commit — M7 `test_m7_corpus` under `tools/ci.sh`.
- [44] plan-driven control (WBC consumes a PreviewWindow) / [45] preview mandate — M3, type-enforced (no default-constructible PreviewWindow).
- [46] two-rate cascade, exactly one structure (SplineSet) crosses the boundary — M3/M4 worlds.
- [47] L0/L1/L2 layering — M2/M3/M4.
- [48] canonical ascending-id ordering — every world's HashRegistry; no container-iteration nondeterminism.
- [49] the tick hash covers controller state (GaitFsm), not just physics — M6 proves it is load-bearing; M7 hashes escalation stream + gait clock too.
- [56] preview never empty (illegal-empty unrepresentable) — M4 (b), type + runtime assert.
- [57] recovery ladder L0 absorb / L1 in-stride / L2 escalate, source-agnostic — M3/M5; the ordering absorb < in-stride < escalate is the invariant, reproduced by the corpus.
Seams frozen at stub fidelity: S1–S6, S8 (S8 provisional). DEFERRED to later
phases (NOT this slice): S7 command-bus/300 ms delay (A4), Jolt substitution
(A3, S4 real impl), terrain/Lua/UE (Phase B+). No RNG yet ([3] seed pinned/unused).

**Serves (Tier 1):** «The Hand That Isn't Yours» — where the fast-band reflexes come from: dojo-
trained policies become the pilot's "spinal lightning," deployed through N1's socket.

## The three tiers (training-doc §1)
| Tier | Engine | Property |
|---|---|---|
| RUNTIME | simcore (Jolt + SDF, CPU) | cross-machine bit-deterministic — the world's law |
| DOJO | MuJoCo/MJX (GPU-parallel) | run-to-run reproducible, not portable — heavy training |
| REFERENCE | MuJoCo (CPU, seeded) | bit-stable oracle — cross-validates the Servo System & twin |

## The escalation ladder (roadmap §25 — cheapest first; N4 telemetry decides when to stop)
1. **System ID** — fit dojo params (contact/friction/armature/damping) to Jolt rollouts; data
   is free and unlimited; expected to close most of the gap.
2. **Domain randomization** around the fitted point.
3. **Jolt episodes in the training mix** (D-T3's fine-tune, promoted into the dojo).
4. **Residual/adapter net** (the "second neural net" bridging I/O) — ONLY if a persistent
   measured gap remains after 1–3.

## Load-bearing walls & decisions (training-doc §2–§3)
- **Walls:** (1) twin fidelity, (2) obs/act contract, (3) fine-tune throughput floor. Wall 4
  (deterministic inference) is **DELETED** by the server-realtime revision — solvers run
  server-side, only outputs are recorded, so float/GPU nets deploy as-is (Rev-2 §6).
- **D-T2:** policies emit **setpoints** (native currency, #0038 Wire 1 uplink) — deploy as meat
  scripts or firmware with no protocol change; torque-output is the permitted expert path.
- **D-T4:** REFERENCE tolerance tiers — tight for kinematic/servo tracking, statistical-only for
  contact-rich (the solver gap is real and permanent; locomotion transfers, melee needs simcore
  fine-tuning). Alarms per tier so the oracle doesn't cry wolf on melee.

## Sequencing
First artifact = N3's MJCF + schema backends (D-T1), then a single locomotion policy end-to-end
(dojo → deploy → simcore walk) as the pipeline's own exit test. **The walking-policy scaffold
(MJCF twin export + gym env for the capsule/B1 mech) may begin as soon as an N3 twin exists —
it no longer waits for Phase B** (Rev-2 §6).

# #0033 — Spec: the Rev-2 mech bus — permissioned channel pub/sub (supersedes the narrow S7 framing)
type: amendment-proposal        status: closed
refs: [S7] [44] [45] [A4] [PhaseB]   opened: Rev2-design   closed-by: ratified by DayZee 2026-08-09 (Phase-A close batch; MODEL adopted, full-channel BUILD → Phase B)
deps: informs #0010; informs #0030; informs #0031; informs #0032

The Rev-2 bus specification (DayZee design session, 2026-08-08). Generalises the narrow
"command bus" (S7, #0030) into the mech's one data fabric: a **permissioned, channel-
based publish/subscribe bus** carrying BOTH sensor data and commands. This is the model
the script layer, the pilot, and every device attach to. Supersedes the `PlanIntent`/setpoint/
shove framing of #0030 (that becomes a subset) and **resolves #0031**.

## 1. Why a bus (and why not a blackboard)
This is the mature vehicle/robot pattern (CAN, ROS-style pub/sub). It is the right choice
HERE specifically because the bus's two properties are GAME MECHANICS, not plumbing:
- **bandwidth** is a resource (SENSOR/signal substance buys more) — bus congestion is real;
- **permissions** are the capture/privacy axis ([44]) and "no free omniscience" ([45]).
A shared-state blackboard is simpler but hides exactly these two — you'd bolt them back on.
A message bus makes them first-class. So the bus is chosen on game merits, not convention.

## 2. The model — channel pub/sub
```
THE MECH BUS = permissioned channels + publishers/subscribers + bandwidth
│
├─ CHANNELS (typed)
│   ├─ SENSOR    proprio / IMU / contact  (·radar / SDF-rangefind / thermal — Phase B)
│   ├─ ACTUATOR  servo setpoints (SetpointSpline), device commands (launcher-fire, thrust)
│   ├─ GOAL      targets/intent handed to a net ("engage that", "walk there")
│   └─ CONTROL   script/net control (activate / deactivate / configure an endpoint)
│
├─ PRINCIPALS (publish and/or subscribe)
│   pilot · NeuroScripts/nets · stock scripts · devices. Scripts/nets are ADDRESSABLE
│   endpoints — they emit on some channels AND are controllable via CONTROL channels.
│
├─ PERMISSIONS  per principal, per channel, read/write. Capturing silicon = acquiring its
│               channel access; you have no enemy-position channel unless a sensor of
│               yours publishes it. [44][45] made literal.
│
└─ BANDWIDTH    a principal's total channel traffic is metered = SENSOR/signal substance.
```

## 2b. Priority, engagement & suppression — the dynamic layer over permissions
PERMISSIONS (§2) are STATIC grants: may a principal read/write a channel at all. On top of
them sits a DYNAMIC priority/ownership layer — what decides who actually drives a channel
when more than one may, and what lets a high-priority role LOCK OUT the lower ones:

- **Priority.** Each writer carries a per-(source, channel) priority rank, assigned by role
  through the SuperAdmin metaTooling device.
- **Engagement / lease (the key point).** A role/script can ENGAGE. While engaged it **HOLDS**
  its target channels at its priority and **PROHIBITS every lower-priority source** from those
  channels — **whether or not it is emitting anything that tick** — until it DISENGAGES. This
  is NOT "highest active writer wins per tick"; the engaged role OWNS (leases) the channels for
  the whole engagement window and suppresses everything beneath it, silent or not.
  - Example: the **melee fighting net**, once engaged, holds the locomotion channels and blocks
    the **navigation net** AND an **emergency-balance net** (both lower priority) — even on the
    ticks the melee net emits nothing. Nothing lower sneaks in. (This is exactly why the
    withdrawn "floor emergency override" stays withdrawn: an engaged higher role owns it; the
    emergency balance does not get to interrupt a committed melee.)
  - Higher- or specific-priority sources may still preempt a held channel; disengagement releases
    the hold and lower sources resume.
- This is the ownership/claim idea (#0029), living here as the bus's arbitration model.

**Model here, mechanism there:** this section is the MODEL; the **ControlMatrix (#0036)**
IMPLEMENTS it — v1 is the degenerate per-tick case (no engagement, highest active writer wins);
v2 adds engage / hold / suppress / disengage over channel-sets, plus the metaTooling device that
sets the roles/priorities. Keep the two consistent — a change to one changes the other.

## 3. The determinism model — only ACTUATOR channels are the recorded stream
The bus is the addressing+permission fabric for ALL traffic, but **determinism/recording
is a property of WHICH channels are recorded, not of the bus being one thing**:
```
  SENSOR channels ─ derived from the deterministic sim state; read by the script layer;
                    NOT in the recorded stream (a replica regenerates its own sensor
                    views from replicated state). Sensor sim may be non-deterministic
                    server-side [Rev 2 §3] precisely because it is not replicated.
  GOAL channels   ─ pilot→net (held H) + other script layer inputs; NOT recorded (script layer input).
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ACTUATOR chans  ─ setpoint splines + device commands = THE recorded/replicated executed
                    stream. DETERMINISTIC. Replicas replay these; this is the client==server
                    fidelity gate.  ← bit-determinism from here through to gamestate.
```
This keeps BOTH "sensors on the bus" and "sensor sim need not be deterministic" true, with
no fudge: sensors are bus traffic derivable from sim state; only actuation is recorded.

## 4. The script layer is cleanly a bus endpoint
The script layer (server-side, non-deterministic, float/GPU) **subscribes** {SENSOR channels,
its GOAL channel} and **publishes** {ACTUATOR channels: SetpointSplines, later device
commands}. Its reads are not recorded; its writes are. **The frozen S3 `SetpointSpline`
is exactly the script layer→sim boundary** (the ACTUATOR-channel payload for locomotion). So
`wbc`/`stepper`/`ladder` (the setpoint-computing controllers) live on the SCRIPTS side;
the in-sim deterministic stack is bus → control tree → stock servo (L0) → physics.

## 5. What this settles
- **#0031 RESOLVED (closes when built):** "roles editable via delayed commands through
  the bus" = a write to a CONTROL channel addressed to the target endpoint. Not a special
  mechanism — one of the channel types.
- **#0030 (S7 freeze) superseded in framing:** S7 is "the mech bus" per this spec; the
  `PlanIntent`/setpoint/shove of the current `command_bus` is the minimal subset. S7 does
  not freeze until the bus reflects this model (still on HOLD).
- **Sensor API = channels:** script layer v0 subscribes proprio/IMU/contact.

## 6. v0 scope (what to build now vs later)
- **Build now (script layer v0):** channels + endpoints + the read/write (pub/sub) model, exercised
  by the walking slice — pilot GOAL (held H) → walking-net endpoint (subscribes SENSOR+GOAL,
  publishes SetpointSpline) → servo endpoint → physics. `SERVO_SETPOINT` payload becomes a
  `SetpointSpline`. One controllable net endpoint (proves the CONTROL-channel/#0031 pattern).
- **Structural-but-NOT-enforced now (→ Phase B combat/capture/economy):** permission gating
  and bandwidth metering. The channels carry an owner/permission field and a notional cost,
  but nothing is denied or metered until there is combat, capture, and a signal economy.
- **Not built (Phase B):** device/weapon channels (launcher-fire, thrust), radar/SDF/thermal
  sensor channels, multi-net hierarchies.

## Requested action
Human sign-off to adopt §2–§4 as the Rev-2 bus model (supersedes #0030's framing; resolves
#0031 in principle). On sign-off, script layer v0 (§6) builds onto it.

---

## RATIFIED by DayZee Christopher Reay, 2026-08-09 (Phase-A close batch).
§2–§4 (the permissioned channel pub/sub MODEL, the priority/engagement/suppression layer
§2b, and the actuator-only recording determinism model §3) are the adopted Rev-2 bus model.
The narrow S7 `command_bus` (PlanIntent/setpoint/shove) is its minimal subset.

**This ratifies the MODEL; the full-channel IMPLEMENTATION is a Phase B build item.** §6's
"build now" (SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL as first-class channels; actuator-only recording
made literal) was NOT built in Phase A — the walking slice used the minimal subset + the
ControlMatrix (#0036 v1). Building the first-class channels is A4.1's deferred half, re-homed
to Phase B (#0011); **S7 (#0030) freezes when that lands** — not before, because until then
the bus surface is not final. Permission gating + bandwidth metering stay structural-not-
enforced until Phase B combat/capture/economy (§6). This spec is the bus's design-of-record
going into Phase B.

# #0038 — Spec: the wire — data structures crossing component boundaries
type: spec        status: open
refs: [2] [3] [5] [23] [44] [45] [S3] [S4] [S7]   opened: nexii-roadmap   closed-by: <human sign-off>
deps: informs #0011; informs #0030; informs #0036

Design-of-record answering DayZee's question: **what data structures actually go over the
wire between components?** Grounded in the seams already built (S3 `SetpointSpline`, S4
`IBodyState`, the `IScript` contract #0036, `ActuatorFrame`/`ServoReplica`, `ReplayFile`),
not invented. Companion to the Rev-2 bus spec (#0033) and the roadmap's Nexus 1 (ControlMatrix
= sockets) and Nexus 3 (blueprint compiler = the schema source).

## The constraint chain this spec descends from (lived experience → component → design)
Per the project's spec method, the wire is not an engineering convenience — each boundary
exists to make a specific beat of the pilot's lived experience (`the_delay_a_pilots_story.md`)
true. The three wires fall out of three of those beats:

| Lived-experience beat (Tier 1) | The constraint it imposes (Tier 2) | The wire that satisfies it (Tier 3) |
|---|---|---|
| **"Reading"** — *"Nobody sees scripts… all that ever escapes is behavior"*; the whole sport is studying an opponent's hidden reflexes | scripts' I/O must be **private/secret forever**; only committed *behavior* is public and **auditable byte-for-byte** (replay study, prize integrity) | **Wire 1 private + Wire 2 public/recorded** — the private/public cut across the resolution seam IS "behavior is all that escapes" (constraints 23, 3, 33; design §5) |
| **"The Hand That Isn't Yours"** — the stock parry fires below the waterline of awareness, in a band her waking mind can never enter | the fast band is a **separate substrate** reading sensors and emitting actions off-sim, on a deadline, physics-not-rules enforcing commitment | **Wire 1** (the script socket: obs down, action up, deadline = last-setpoints-hold) (constraints 23, 44, 45) |
| **"Three Tenths" / "Letters to the Future"** — the Delay is *fixed*, therefore *learnable*; you mail whole commitments to the mech that will exist | the executed stream must be **deterministic and replicable** so every client lives in one learnable, jitter-free world | **Wire 2** (the resolved actuator stream + hash = the one replicated truth) (constraints 2–5) |
| **"Her Own Body"** — *"a budget that walks"*; every block a sentence, all drawing on one tank | the mech is **one authored source** compiling to every downstream need; mass/torque **emerge** from the build, never hand-set | **Wire 3** (the blueprint → 4 backends + derived schema) (constraints 13–14, 27; roadmap N3) |

So: **Wire 1 is the subconscious band made literal; Wire 2 is the one shared learnable world; Wire 3
is the walking budget compiled.** Everything below designs these three to satisfy exactly those.

## 0. Framing — "over the wire" = a serialized payload crossing a process/host/machine boundary
The engine has exactly **three** such boundaries, and the roadmap's socket decision (Nexus 1)
makes them literal transports rather than in-process calls. They are told apart by ONE
property — their **determinism status** — because that is what decides whether their bytes are
load-bearing, recorded, replicated, and public:

```
THE WIRE — three boundaries, cut by determinism status
│
├─ WIRE 1  Script socket        ControlMatrix ⇄ Script process   bidirectional · per-tick
│          NON-deterministic · NOT recorded · owner-PRIVATE · METERED (socket = the meter)
│          "the obs/act contract" — the realtime control loop
│
├─ WIRE 2  Replica broadcast    Server → Client replica          one-way · per-tick
│          DETERMINISTIC · RECORDED (= the replay file) · PUBLIC · the fidelity/cheat gate
│          "the executed actuator stream" — the ONLY determinism-load-bearing bytes
│
└─ WIRE 3  Blueprint artifacts  Spec compiler → {4 backends}      once per design · not live
           the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH; derives the SCHEMAS that Wire 1 & Wire 2 conform to
           (+ WIRE 4, Phase C: sim → UE snapshot — one-way, read-only, display-only, unrecorded)
```

The whole determinism argument of Framework Rev 2 reduces to one sentence about this diagram:
**only Wire 2's bytes are replicated and hashed; Wire 1 and the sensor sim behind it are free
to be float/GPU/non-deterministic because nothing downstream of the sim replays them.**

## 1. The unifying atom — one channel message
Every live-wire payload is the uniform command form (implementation-plan constraint 9),
addressed to a **channel** (the Rev-2 bus, #0033):

```cpp
struct ChannelMsg {                    // the atom on WIRE 1 (both ways) and WIRE 2
    uint32_t  principal_id;            // who: pilot · script/net · device · autonomic-repair
    uint32_t  channel_id;              // where: a SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL channel (#0033 §2)
    int32_t   priority;                // the arbitration rank (#0033 §2b, #0036)
    uint64_t  effective_tick;          // when it executes (issue + H for held pilot intent; else now)
    uint8_t   lease;                   // 0=one-shot · 1=ENGAGE (hold+suppress) · 2=DISENGAGE (#0033 §2b)
    Payload   payload;                 // TYPED BY THE CHANNEL KIND — see below
};
```
`payload` is a discriminated union keyed by the channel's kind:

| Channel kind | Payload type | Built? |
|---|---|---|
| `SENSOR`   | a sample record (proprio/IMU/contact; later ray/radar/thermal) | proprio via S4 `IBodyState` |
| `ACTUATOR` | `SetpointSpline` (S3), **or** a device command, **or** raw torque (expert path) | `SplineSet` built |
| `GOAL`     | `PlanIntent` / a target handed to a net | `PlanIntent` built |
| `CONTROL`  | endpoint command: activate/deactivate/configure/engage another endpoint | seam only (#0031) |

Everything below is this atom, specialised per wire.

---

## 2. WIRE 1 — the Script socket (the obs/act contract)
> *Serves «The Hand That Isn't Yours» + «Meat»: the subconscious band made literal — a private
> substrate reading sensors and emitting actions off-sim, metered at the socket.*

The realtime control loop. The ControlMatrix (server-side) hosts each script as a **separate
process connected by a socket** (Nexus 1 decision); the socket is both the isolation boundary
(a crashed/overrunning script just misses its deadline; its last setpoints hold) and the
metering boundary (compute is billed at the socket, not simulated as packets). Per tick, for
each hosted script:

**Downlink — the Observation frame (ControlMatrix → script):** the SENSOR + GOAL channels the
script is permitted to subscribe, snapshotted from live authoritative state. This is exactly
the argument of the built contract `IScript::produce(const IBodyState& obs, uint64_t tick)`.
```cpp
struct ObservationFrame {              // WIRE 1 downlink — NOT recorded, NOT replicated
    uint64_t tick;
    // SENSOR channels (v1 = the S4 body-state seam; the A4.3 neural script flattens this to
    //   12 doubles: com pos/vel, com height, angular momentum, support half-width, 2 feet):
    BodyStateSnapshot sensors;         // proprio/IMU/contact now; +ray/radar/thermal in Phase B
    // GOAL channel (pilot intent handed to this net, already held H ticks at the server):
    PlanIntent goal;
    // the script keeps its OWN recurrent hidden state process-side between calls — NOT sent.
};
```
Derived from deterministic sim state, but the **sensor simulation itself need not be
deterministic** (#0033 §3, Rev-2 §3): it is never recorded, so a replica regenerates its own
sensor views from replicated state and never needs to match the server's sensor bytes.

**Uplink — the Action frame (script → ControlMatrix):** the ACTUATOR + CONTROL channel writes
the script publishes. This is the built `ScriptOutput`, plus the CONTROL writes (#0031):
```cpp
struct ActionFrame {                   // WIRE 1 uplink — script's writes; recorded ONLY after resolution
    bool      active;                  // deadline flag: false ⇒ produced nothing ⇒ last write holds
    bool      writes[AC_COUNT];        // which ACTUATOR channels carry a fresh value this tick
    SplineSet splines;                 // the S3 setpoint payload for the channels it wrote
    // + (Phase B) device commands (launcher-fire, thrust) and CONTROL writes (engage/config
    //   another endpoint) as additional ChannelMsgs — the seam is open, not built.
};
```
**Metering / privacy:** the script's reads and writes on Wire 1 are **owner-private, never
shipped**. Only after the ControlMatrix RESOLVES the actuator channels (per-channel priority
/ engagement, #0036/#0033 §2b) do the *resolved* writes cross to Wire 2. The conflict channel,
the scripts' I/O, and the priority policy stay server-side.

**Location-transparency is already proven.** The A4.3 neural script (`loco/neural_script.h`)
serialises `obs`→`double[N_OBS]` and `action`→`double[N_ACT]` and shows the marshalled path is
bit-identical to the direct call. Wire 1 is that seam over a socket; no new semantics.

---

## 3. WIRE 2 — the Replica broadcast (the executed actuator stream)
> *Serves «Three Tenths»/«Letters» + «Reading»: the one fixed, learnable, shared world — and the
> only thing public, so "behavior is all that escapes" and every winning run is auditable byte-exact.*

The replication wire and the **only determinism-load-bearing bytes in the system**. Per tick
the server ships the **resolved ACTUATOR-channel writes** (one value per channel after
arbitration) and nothing else about control. A deterministic replica replays exactly these
through `servo_batch → physics` and reproduces server body state bit-for-bit; a per-tick state
hash is the replica-fidelity (and cheat-detection) gate. This is the built `ActuatorFrame`:
```cpp
struct ActuatorFrame {                 // WIRE 2 per-tick — RECORDED, REPLICATED, PUBLIC
    SplineSet splines;                 // S3 servo-channel writes (the resolved winners)
    FootState feet[2];                 // ⚠ leg-less-mech artifact (#0034) — see note
    Vec3      shove_impulse;           // world-authored disturbance this tick (N·s), if any
    bool      has_shove;
    // + the executed pilot intent that came due at this tick (the held PlanIntent), when one did.
};
```
Its **durable form** is the replay file — the recorded stream plus the pinning metadata that
makes a replay a versioned, auditable artifact (constraint 3, prize-league integrity):
```cpp
struct ReplayFile {
    uint32_t             format_version;
    std::string          scenario_id;
    uint64_t             seed;
    std::string          sim_version_tag;   // engine/Jolt pinning — a mismatch is a hard stop
    std::vector<Command> commands;          // the executed stream (issue-tick records)
};
struct HashLog { std::vector<uint64_t> hashes; };  // per-tick digest — equality IS the regression test
```
**What is NOT on Wire 2** (the negative space is the whole privacy/determinism argument):
sensor channels (a replica regenerates its own — Wire 1 downlink), GOAL channels (script
input), the conflict channel and priority policy (owner-private, #0036), and the script's
internal state (`GaitFsm`, net hidden state — server-side only; the replica has none, #0034).

> ⚠ **`feet[2]` is a known limitation, not the design (#0034).** A leg-less/stub mech places
> feet by poking body state directly — not a channel write — so a replica replaying channel
> writes never receives it and diverges at the first step. On an **articulated** mech (B1.2
> shipped the walk; **B1.3** makes it replica-faithful) there is no separate foot output: swing
> and plant are joint setpoints (already ACTUATOR writes) and touchdown is an ordinary contact
> event physics computes identically everywhere. B1.3 deletes `feet[2]` from Wire 2. Until then
> our mechs are replica-faithful for STANDING, not WALKING (experimentally confirmed, #0034).

---

## 4. WIRE 3 — the Blueprint artifacts (Nexus 3, the schema source)
> *Serves «Her Own Body»: the "budget that walks" compiled — one authored source from which
> mass, torque, and the obs/act channels all EMERGE, never hand-set.*

Not a live per-tick wire but the artifact that crosses every tool boundary and, crucially,
**derives the schemas Wire 1 and Wire 2 must conform to**. One blueprint (the anatomy material
field) compiles to four backends (roadmap Nexus 3 / training-doc D-T1):
```
BLUEPRINT (anatomy field, int16 fixed-point per units-charter §3)
├─ (a) simcore/Jolt bodies + servo config   → what Wire 2 actuates (joint tree, gains, limits)
├─ (b) SDF material field                    → narrowphase/contact + damage diff (Phase B)
├─ (c) MJCF twin                             → the dojo (Nexus 5 training); kinematic twin of (a)
├─ (d) game/UI metadata                      → builder, HUD, economy costing
└─ (derived) OBS/ACT SCHEMA                  → the channel list/types/ordering for WIRE 1 & 2,
                                               from the nerve-bandwidth static analysis (24/43),
                                               NEVER hand-written
```
The crosscutting point: **Nexus 3 is upstream of both live wires.** The obs/act schema is the
one place the SENSOR channel set (Wire 1 downlink), the ACTUATOR channel set (Wire 1 uplink =
Wire 2 payload), and the channel ordering used by every hash are all defined together, from the
mech's actual routed nervous system. Today these shapes are hand-cut (12-double obs, 4 servo
channels); Nexus 3 replaces the hand-cutting with derivation, and the twin (c) is what makes
the schema checkable across engines (training-doc Walls 1–2).

---

## 5. Crosscutting dimensions (factor out time; three orthogonal cuts)
```
                    WIRE 1 (script socket)     WIRE 2 (replica cast)     WIRE 3 (blueprint)
determinism   ┃     non-deterministic          DETERMINISTIC            compile-time exact
recording     ┃     never recorded             IS the replay file       versioned artifact
privacy       ┃     owner-PRIVATE (secret)     PUBLIC (shippable)       public (the design)
direction     ┃     bidirectional              one-way (server→replica) one-way (source→backends)
cadence       ┃     per-tick (or per-N)        per-tick                 per-design-change
metered?      ┃     YES (socket = the meter)   no (fixed executed set)  no
```
Cross-over points worth naming:
- **The resolution seam** is where Wire 1 becomes Wire 2: the ControlMatrix takes many private
  `ActionFrame`s, arbitrates per channel, and emits one public `ActuatorFrame`. Private→public
  and non-deterministic→deterministic happen at the *same* point — that is why the ControlMatrix
  is the natural home of both (Nexus 1).
- **The schema seam** is where Wire 3 constrains Wires 1&2: change the mech's nerve routing →
  recompile → the obs/act channel set on both live wires changes. One edit, both wires move.
- **The privacy axis (design §5)** falls straight out: Wire 1 = brain (secret, off-sim,
  burnable); Wire 2 = the public simulated world (capturable). "Capture the silicon" = acquire
  its channel permissions on the bus — a Wire-2/permission fact, not a special mechanism.

## 6. Build status (what exists vs what the wire still needs)
- **Built & proven in-process:** `IScript::produce` (Wire 1 shape, remotable seam);
  A4.3 marshal seam (obs/act serialize bit-identical to direct call); `ActuatorFrame` +
  `ServoReplica` (Wire 2 replay, bit-identical for stand); `ReplayFile`/`HashLog` + the M7
  corpus CI gate; ControlMatrix v1 per-channel resolution (#0036) = the Wire1→Wire2 seam.
- **Open / Phase-B (the standing work, re-homed under the nexii, #0039):**
  1. **Socket transport** for Wire 1 (currently in-process function objects) — Nexus 1.
  2. **First-class channel messages** (`ChannelMsg` with SENSOR/ACTUATOR/GOAL/CONTROL) —
     today Wire 2 is the 4 servo channels only; the full bus is #0033 §6 / A4.1's deferred half.
     **S7 (#0030) freezes when this lands.**
  3. **B1.3** — articulated replica-faithful walk; deletes `feet[2]` from `ActuatorFrame` (#0034).
  4. **Sensor channels** beyond proprio (contact/ray/radar/thermal) on Wire 1 — Phase B.
  5. **The obs/act schema derivation** (Wire 3) — needs the Nexus 3 blueprint compiler.
  6. **Permission + bandwidth fields** carried-but-not-enforced until combat/capture/economy.

## Requested action
Human sign-off that §0–§5 are the wire model of record (the three boundaries, the determinism/
privacy/schema cuts, and `ChannelMsg`/`ObservationFrame`/`ActionFrame`/`ActuatorFrame` as the
payload families). On sign-off this becomes the contract the Nexus 1 socket build and the Nexus 3
schema derivation implement, and the reference for S7's eventual freeze (#0030).
